plans.summary: Revision plan for cutting ASSEMBLY-CONNECTION-PLAN-2026-07-27.md (WS-1) into work packages. Verified the plan against repo ground truth and found four repo contradictions the plan asserts as settled: (1) the doorway router has no path or query parameters at all and server.py discards the query string, so Part B's per-run reads and Part C's `GET /runs/contract` are unroutable today — meaning Part C's "one server.py change (bytes out)" is at least two, not one; (2) `cw.run`'s INSERT policy in 0005 carries no agreement-ownership condition, so Part A's claim that "the database's row-level security decides whether that deal is the caller's" is false as the schema stands — honouring the SETTLED "runs are tied to deals" decision without putting permission logic in an endpoint requires migration 0024; (3) `cw.run` already has an AFTER INSERT trigger emitting `run_recorded`, so Part A step 6's endpoint-side `run_recorded` would double-record the same act; (4) `cw.run_snapshot`, the reproducibility view Part C reaches for, is granted to `cw_auditor` only — the rebuild must read base tables. Proposed cut: eight single-owner packages WP-001..WP-008, A split as the plan permits plus one hoisted transport package that removes server.py/app.py from the critical path of B, C and D. Every Part A-F is covered; F lives inside each package; the three named mutation-harness additions land in WP-005 (rebuild-before-build) and WP-006 (expiry re-check, gate check); the service-level round trip lands in WP-005 where both endpoints first coexist.

diagnosis: Parts A, C and D each need multi-step orchestration inside one transaction (engine calls plus several statements), which the existing reads.Read / writes.Write single-statement shapes cannot express. They must follow the manifests.py precedent: a new module per part plus one dispatch line in app.py. That is a clean package boundary and makes app.py a shared file across three packages — safe only because A->C->D is already serial.

Part B maps cleanly onto reads.py's existing Read shape ONLY if the reads stay parameterless. Every one of the 24 existing READS is parameterless and reads.run() passes no params; cw.run_decision and cw.run_finding are RLS-scoped through cw.run, so parameterless run reads are both viable and in-house-style. This should be stated as the package's decision rather than left implicit, because the plan's phrasing ('GET /runs/decisions') reads as per-run.

Part C cannot be a single bounded change to server.py as the plan claims. Producing a .docx for A run requires naming the run, and the router does exact-match on method+path with no path segments or query string. Both the bytes-out change and a routing/parameter change land in server.py and app.py. Left inside Part C, those transport changes sit on the critical path behind A and B for no reason and force C to be simultaneously a transport package and a document package.

Part A's deal-binding step rests on a database rule that does not exist. cw.run's write_scoped INSERT policy checks role only. The settled decision 'runs are tied to deals' therefore has no enforcement behind it, and hard constraint 2 forbids fixing it in the endpoint. This is a genuine need for migration 0024 discovered by a Part, exactly as plan section 4 anticipates — but the plan's section 1 states flatly that no migration is expected, so the contradiction must be surfaced and owned by a named package.

Part A step 6's audit event collides with the schema. cw.run already carries an AFTER INSERT trigger (audit_run) that emits run_recorded with vendor, snapshot, ruleset, result_hash, gate_open, overridden, manifest_source and engine_version. An endpoint-side _record('run_recorded') would write a second, weaker copy of the same fact into an append-only chain that can never be corrected. The endpoint's job is the REFUSAL and ATTEMPT half only.

Part C's audit step has an unstated access consequence. Recording document_produced inside the caller's own transaction is correct by the manifests.py uniformity rule, but INSERT on cw.audit_event is granted only to requester, legal_reviewer and legal_admin. An auditor may read every run and will be refused the download, by the chain rather than by the run. That is defensible and possibly right, but it is a decision, not a detail, and it must be recorded in the package rather than discovered by an auditor.

Part C's rebuild source is mis-specified. cw.run_snapshot is the view built for exactly this purpose but its SELECT grant goes to cw_auditor alone; requester, legal_reviewer and legal_admin hold grants on the base tables cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member and cw.snapshot_ladder_rung. A package that reaches for the obvious view will get a 403 for every role that is supposed to be able to pull paper.

Part D is the largest part and carries three separable concerns: the insert set (four tables, freeze triggers, status machine), the expiry re-check, and the validation gate. It should stay one package anyway, because splitting it would let a half-built execute endpoint exist that files an agreement without one of its two gates — a worse failure mode than a large package. Its size is managed by the two named mutations, not by cutting it.

Part D has an unnamed hard requirement: cw.executed_document.storage_uri is NOT NULL with no default, and the byte store that would supply it is WS-8, explicitly out of scope. Settled decision 2 covers hash and signatories and says nothing about storage_uri. The package must record what it writes there and why that is honest rather than a placeholder pretending to be a location.

Part D's two gates are business logic in an endpoint. That does not violate hard constraint 2 (which forbids PERMISSION logic), but it is the first such logic in the doorway and the plan does not say so out loud. The alternative — a trigger in a new migration — is real and should be considered and rejected in writing by the package, not silently skipped.

Part E cannot be a single package that stays single-owner. It touches prototype/v4/app/api.jsx, shell.jsx, workspaces.jsx, requester.jsx and reviewer.jsx, plus db/test/shell.test.mjs and db/test/mutation-check.mjs; and the plan itself splits its timing (screens after B, execute screen after D). Two packages with an explicit prerequisite edge is the only cut that keeps every file single-owner-at-a-time.

Part E has a shell-level cost the plan does not mention: the requester tab set in shell.jsx contains no manifest, run or document tab, shell.test.mjs holds an INDEPENDENT copy of that specification, and mutation-check.mjs's shell block asserts the tab<->pane bijection. Adding a pane means three coordinated edits in one package, or a red bar.

Part E also collides with a stated control in api.jsx: reads take no parameters, and the reading-room comment argues that a parameter is precisely how broad-fetch-and-filter creeps back in. A run view needs to name a run. The screens package must state the distinction (a run is the caller's own artefact identified by a server-generated id, not a share scoped by identity) rather than quietly adding an argument.

Part F is correctly placed inside every part, but the plan under-counts the harnesses: npm run verify runs three (db/test/mutation-check.mjs, engine/mutation_check.py, doorway/mutation_check.py). The plan says 'both existing mutation harnesses'. Packages must be told all three stay green, and which one each addition belongs in.

The plan's 'round trip that matters most' already has an engine-level namesake in db/test/writer-sql.test.mjs (snapshot_rows -> insert -> read back -> snapshot_from_rows, id unchanged). The service-level version the plan asks for is genuinely different and must be named as such, or a reviewer will see the existing green test and believe it is done.

Two smaller factual drifts: the plan says Part A loads 'cw.conflict_rule rows into a RuleSet' while the engine's own RULE_SQL reads cw.active_conflict_rule (retired and future-dated rules excluded); and manifests.manifest_from accepts any string for `source` while cw.run.manifest_source is constrained to ('llm','fallback','manual'), so a stray source value becomes a 409 IntegrityError instead of the 400 the house pattern reserves for caller mistakes.

cw.run_drift (0022) and cw.run_origin_mix (0009) both exist, are run-scoped, and are unmentioned anywhere in the plan. run_drift in particular already computes exactly the in-flight expiry/supersession comparison Part D's expiry gate describes, joined on the pinned (clause_id, version). Part D should consult it rather than write a fresh comparison.
symptoms: The plan states Part C's bytes-out change 'is the only change this plan makes outside adding endpoints and screens', while both Part B and Part C in fact require the router to be able to name a run.
The plan states in section 1 that 'no migration is expected', while the settled deal-binding decision has no database rule to enforce it.
Part A step 6 names run_recorded as an endpoint act, while the schema already emits that exact event from a trigger.
Part C step 1 says 'read the stored snapshot members ... back through the caller's connection' without naming a source, and the one view built for it is auditor-only.
The plan's decision list (section 5) is closed, yet Part D depends on a NOT NULL storage_uri that no settled decision covers.
Part B is described in per-run language ('GET /runs/decisions') against a read layer that has never carried a parameter.
Part E is described as one part while its timing is already split (screens after B, execute screen after D) and its files overlap.
Part F says 'both existing mutation harnesses' where the verify script runs three.
consequences: If the transport gap is not hoisted out, WP for Part C becomes two packages wearing one name, and server.py/app.py get edited under time pressure at the point in the sequence where the most is already built on top of them.

If the cw.run ownership gap is not owned by a package, WS-1 ships an endpoint where a requester can attach a run to another requester's deal, and the audit chain will record it as legitimate — the failure mode the whole permission model exists to prevent, arriving through the one write the model never constrained.

If the endpoint also writes run_recorded, the append-only chain gains two entries per run that disagree in detail, and no correction is possible: cw.audit_event has no UPDATE or DELETE grant for any role.

If Part C selects from cw.run_snapshot, every role that is meant to be able to download will get a 403 whose sentence names a view rather than the act, and the natural fix (grant the view more widely) quietly widens what an auditor-only reproducibility surface exposes.
If the auditor/download consequence is not recorded, an auditor's refusal will read as a bug at the worst moment — during the acceptance sweep WP-U15 depends on.

If Part D's gates are written without deciding endpoint-versus-trigger in writing, the next person to add an execution path (WS-6's close-of-negotiation seam) will have no rule to follow and will pick differently.
If Part E lands as one package, either api.jsx/shell.jsx get two owners at once or the execute screen waits on the requester screens for no reason beyond packaging.
If the service-level round trip is not distinguished from writer-sql.test.mjs, the plan's most load-bearing test is scored as already passing.
proposed_actions: Cut WS-1 into eight single-owner packages, WP-001..WP-008, in this dependency order: WP-001 -> WP-002 -> WP-003 -> WP-004 -> {WP-005 -> WP-006, WP-007}; WP-008 requires both WP-006 and WP-007. This preserves plan section 3's A->B->C->D chain exactly, honours 'E after B, execute screen after D', and adds one predecessor (transport) with a recorded reason.

WP-001 · Transport seam (Part C's server change, hoisted). Owner: doorway. Target files: backend/doorway/server.py, backend/doorway/app.py, backend/doorway/test_server.py, backend/doorway/mutation_check.py. Changes: (a) give Response a bytes-capable sibling (status, body-or-bytes, content type, filename) so app.py can express a download without server.py learning about runs; (b) stop discarding the query string in _endpoint() and pass parsed query to App.handle; (c) leave every existing JSON endpoint byte-identical. No engine call, no SQL, no screen. Prerequisites: none.

WP-002 · Part A1: POST /runs wired and refusing. Owner: doorway. Target files: backend/doorway/runs.py (new), backend/doorway/app.py (one dispatch line), backend/doorway/test_runs.py (new), backend/db/test/loader-sql.test.mjs (extend: run the three loader queries as each of the five roles against the migrated schema). Changes: manifests.manifest_from for the body; re-run check_manifest against categories_for; run CLAUSE_SQL/RULE_SQL/LADDER_SQL over the caller's Request; Snapshot.build via loader.build_snapshot; build_ruleset; resolve() then validate(); answer with the run summary shape. NO persistence, no run id. Audit: record the ATTEMPT as run_attempted / run_refused — never run_recorded, which the schema's own trigger owns. Prerequisites: WP-001 (none strictly, but sequenced to keep app.py single-owner).

WP-003 · Part A2: persistence, audit and the deal rule. Owner: doorway + db. Target files: backend/doorway/runs.py, backend/db/migrations/0024_a_run_belongs_to_the_callers_deal.sql (NEW — claims 0024), backend/db/test/run-store.test.mjs, backend/doorway/test_runs.py, backend/doorway/mutation_check.py. Changes: snapshot_rows/ruleset_rows/run_rows inserted through the caller's connection; server-generated run id; agreement_id required by the endpoint; engine_version from engine.model.ENGINE_VERSION; manifest_source validated against the schema's enum in manifest handling so a bad value is a 400 not a 409; provenance counts on the run row. Migration 0024 rewrites cw.run's write_scoped INSERT policy to add `and (agreement_id is null or cw.owns_agreement(agreement_id))`, with the reason recorded in the migration header: the settled decision has no rule behind it and putting one in the endpoint is forbidden. Prerequisites: WP-002.

WP-004 · Part B: read runs back. Owner: doorway + screens-api. Target files: backend/doorway/reads.py (three or four new entries), backend/doorway/test_reads.py, prototype/v4/app/api.jsx (read functions only, no panes). Changes: GET /runs from cw.run_summary, GET /runs/decisions from cw.run_contract, GET /runs/findings from cw.run_finding, and optionally GET /runs/drift from cw.run_drift. All parameterless, scoped by the database, in the reading-room precedent; the package records that choice and its rationale. Prerequisites: WP-003.

WP-005 · Part C: GET /runs/contract. Owner: doorway. Target files: backend/doorway/documents.py (new), backend/doorway/app.py, backend/doorway/test_documents.py (new), backend/doorway/mutation_check.py. Changes: read the stored snapshot from the BASE tables cw.snapshot_member and cw.snapshot_ladder_rung (never cw.run_snapshot, which is auditor-only) plus cw.clause_version; snapshot_from_rows; refuse the download on SnapshotIncomplete or an id mismatch, naming stored and rebuilt ids; build_docx for the bytes; sha256_of for the hash; audit document_produced with the hash; feed the computed hash to cw.record_rebuild_spot_check via the existing POST /health-checks/rebuild path. Record the decision that an auditor cannot download because the chain refuses their insert. Prerequisites: WP-001, WP-004.

WP-006 · Part D: POST /agreements/execute. Owner: doorway. Target files: backend/doorway/executions.py (new), backend/doorway/app.py, backend/doorway/test_executions.py (new), backend/doorway/mutation_check.py, backend/db/test/executed.test.mjs. Changes: insert cw.executed_agreement (run_id, executed_on, effective_on, term_end, agreement_kind), cw.executed_document seq 0 (filename, byte_size, sha256, storage_uri, signed_on), cw.executed_signatory rows, and cw.signature_certificate only when supplied — matching settled decision 2. Expiry gate: for each selected clause in the run, compare the PINNED (clause_id, version) against cw.clause_version_state / cw.run_drift and refuse naming the clause. Validation gate: refuse a run whose gate_open is false unless an override is in force. Audit agreement_executed. The package records, in writing, that these two are business gates rather than permission logic, and why they are not a migration. Prerequisites: WP-005.

WP-007 · Part E1: the requester's screens. Owner: screens. Target files: prototype/v4/app/shell.jsx (requester tab set), prototype/v4/app/workspaces.jsx (PANES entries), prototype/v4/app/requester.jsx (manifest panel, run view, download; retires the NotBuiltYet at line 335 and the 'the forge that produces runs is not built yet' caption), prototype/v4/app/api.jsx (submit/download functions), backend/db/test/shell.test.mjs (its independent copy of the tab specification), backend/db/test/mutation-check.mjs (shell target rows). Prerequisites: WP-004 for the run view and WP-005 for the download.

WP-008 · Part E2: the reviewer's execute screen. Owner: screens. Target files: prototype/v4/app/reviewer.jsx, prototype/v4/app/workspaces.jsx, prototype/v4/app/api.jsx, backend/db/test/shell.test.mjs, backend/db/test/mutation-check.mjs. Changes: run view from Legal's side, the execute action with the evidence fields settled decision 2 requires, refusals shown in the database's and engine's own words. Prerequisites: WP-006 and WP-007.

Place the plan's named mutation-harness additions precisely: 'break the rebuild-before-build' in WP-005 against its own named test in test_documents.py; 'break the expiry re-check' and 'break the gate check' in WP-006 against two named tests in test_executions.py. Each is a row in backend/doorway/mutation_check.py in the existing (name, file, find, replace, the one test that must fail) shape, and each must be seen to go from ok to MISS when removed.

Place the service-level round trip in WP-005, named explicitly as distinct from db/test/writer-sql.test.mjs: record a run through POST /runs as the caller, request the document through GET /runs/contract as the same caller, and assert the rebuilt snapshot id equals the stored one — through the service, not in an engine test.

Reconcile the plan text with the repo in the package headers rather than editing the plan: Part A reads cw.active_conflict_rule (not cw.conflict_rule); npm run verify carries three mutation harnesses (not two); cw.run_drift and cw.run_origin_mix exist and are the natural sources for Part B's drift read and Part D's expiry gate.

Seed synthetic conflict rules as development data inside WP-002 or WP-003 under the placeholder-content rule (CLAUDE.md, memory.md 2026-07-27), so validate() is exercised against a non-empty catalogue and 'zero rules reads as zero' is tested as the OTHER case rather than the only one.
affected_files_or_sections: backend/doorway/server.py (WP-001 only: _respond bytes path, _endpoint query capture)
backend/doorway/app.py (WP-001 Response shape; WP-002, WP-005, WP-006 each add one dispatch line — serial by prerequisite)
backend/doorway/refusals.py (no change expected in any package; classify() already covers 42501, IntegrityError, RaiseException)
backend/doorway/manifests.py (no change; reused by WP-002 via manifest_from and categories_for)
backend/doorway/mutation_check.py (append-only rows: WP-001, WP-003, WP-005, WP-006)
backend/doorway/test_runs.py, test_documents.py, test_executions.py (NEW, one per owning package)
prototype/v4/app/api.jsx (WP-004 reads; WP-007 submit/download; WP-008 execute — serial by prerequisite)
prototype/v4/app/shell.jsx (WP-007; WP-008 only if the reviewer gains a tab)
backend/engine/** (NOT MODIFIED by any package — hard constraint 1)
risks: Migration 0024 in WP-003 contradicts the plan's section-1 statement that no migration is expected. The risk is that a reviewer rejects the package for exceeding the plan rather than reading it as plan section 4's anticipated 'a Part discovers a genuine need'. Mitigation: the migration header states the discovered fact (cw.run's INSERT policy checks role only) and cites hard constraint 2 as why the endpoint cannot fix it.

0024 rewrites an existing policy on a table that already has immutability triggers and administrator_reads from 0013. A CREATE OR REPLACE on the wrong policy name, or dropping and recreating it, could leave cw.run momentarily without a write policy — which fails closed, but would surface as a confusing refusal. Mitigation: run-store.test.mjs must assert both directions (own deal allowed, other's deal refused) as each of the three writing roles.

WP-001's query-string change touches the one file every endpoint passes through. A mistake there is a whole-service outage, not a feature bug. Mitigation: no endpoint consumes the query in WP-001; the parameter is captured and ignored, proven by an unchanged full doorway suite plus a mutation row.

app.py is edited by four packages. The prerequisite chain makes that safe only if the chain is enforced. Mitigation: no two of WP-002/005/006 may be in flight simultaneously; the dispatch lines are additive and adjacent.

api.jsx is edited by three packages (WP-004, WP-007, WP-008) and is the file the 'no broad fetch' rule lives in. Mitigation: WP-004 adds read functions only and no panes, so the file's two rules are re-argued once, not three times.

The expiry gate in WP-006 compares a PINNED clause version against live state. Reading expiry from cw.clause_version_state without joining on version would compare the run's clause against the current version and pass or fail for the wrong reason. Mitigation: use cw.run_drift, which already joins on (clause_id, version), and name the join in the acceptance criteria.

storage_uri is NOT NULL and WS-8 does not exist. Whatever WP-006 records there will look like a real location to every later reader, including cw.execution_evidence_gap. Mitigation: the value's shape and its meaning are recorded in the package and in a schema comment, and the round trip through POST /health-checks/document is explicitly NOT claimed to work until WS-8.

Recording document_produced inside the caller's transaction makes the download unavailable to auditors and viewers. If that is judged wrong later, the alternative (audit outside the caller's transaction) reintroduces a privileged path — the thing db.py exists to make impossible. Mitigation: the decision is recorded as a decision in WP-005, not as an implementation detail.

Part D's two gates are the doorway's first business logic. Every later endpoint author will copy them. Mitigation: WP-006 writes the endpoint-versus-trigger comparison down and the two mutations make the gates falsifiable.

Screens have no rendering test — shell.test.mjs is static analysis over source. WP-007 and WP-008 can be green while the pane is broken in a browser. Mitigation: each screens package carries a recorded browser walk, as WP-U07 did, and does not claim the walk is automated.

npm run verify rebuilds the schema per test and the doorway suite is already reported at roughly four minutes. Adding three doorway mutations and several suites lengthens the bar. Mitigation: the new mutations follow the existing one-named-test-only convention rather than running the whole suite.
acceptance_criteria: Every Part A-F of the plan is covered by at least one package and no Part is covered by two packages that mutate the same file concurrently.

WP-001: a bytes response carries the .docx content type, a filename and a content-length, and every existing endpoint's JSON response is byte-identical before and after; a query string reaches App.handle; one mutation row proves the JSON path is still guarded.

WP-002: a viewer calling POST /runs is refused by the database before the engine's answer is ever reported (the manifests.py uniformity rule), proven by a named test; a manifest with a dropped category refuses with the engine's own sentence exactly as POST /manifests/check does; an empty library refuses loudly with SnapshotIncomplete's words and never returns a partial run; the answer states how many rules were consulted and zero reads as zero; loader-sql.test.mjs runs all three loader queries as each of the five roles against the migrated schema.

WP-003: a requester recording a run against another requester's deal is refused BY THE DATABASE, in the database's words, proven by a named test in test_runs.py and by run-store.test.mjs; exactly one run_recorded event exists per run (the trigger's), and the endpoint's own events are run_attempted / run_refused; cw.run.engine_version equals engine.model.ENGINE_VERSION; a manifest source outside ('llm','fallback','manual') is a 400 with the field named, not a 409; migration 0024 exists, records why it was claimed, and no 0025 is created.

WP-004: GET /runs, /runs/decisions and /runs/findings answer as the caller with no parameter; an auditor sees every run, a requester sees only runs they created or runs on their own deals, a viewer is refused; GET /reading-room/clauses returns rows for the first time against a genuinely recorded run and no fixture fakes one (WP-U15's standing instruction).

WP-005: the document is produced only from a run that just proved it reproduces — a forced id mismatch refuses with both the stored and the rebuilt id in the sentence; build_docx's zero-authored-characters assertion holds and no provenance footer appears on the document; document_produced is recorded with the SHA-256 of the exact bytes returned; nothing is stored; the SERVICE-LEVEL round trip test exists and is named as distinct from db/test/writer-sql.test.mjs — record a run through POST /runs, rebuild through GET /runs/contract, snapshot id must match, as the caller; the 'break the rebuild-before-build' mutation is in doorway/mutation_check.py and its one named test is seen to fail.

WP-006: a requester calling POST /agreements/execute is refused by the database (0006 grants), not by the endpoint; execution refuses when any selected clause's approval has lapsed between run and signature, naming the clause; execution refuses a run whose gate is closed with no override in force; the insert set matches what the hand-inserted demo row inserted and the freeze triggers and status machine are left to do their existing jobs; agreement_executed is recorded; the 'break the expiry re-check' and 'break the gate check' mutations are in doorway/mutation_check.py and each is caught by the test that names it, seen to fail; what storage_uri carries is recorded in the package.

WP-007: the requester's manifest panel pre-flights via the existing POST /manifests/check and submits via POST /runs; the run view shows each decision with its reason, each finding and the gate state; the document downloads; the NotBuiltYet at requester.jsx:335 and the 'the forge that produces runs is not built yet' caption are gone; shell.test.mjs's independent tab specification is updated in the same package and the tab<->pane bijection holds; mutation-check.mjs's shell rows still catch a reintroduced stub; no canned data is added.

WP-008: the reviewer's execute action carries the evidence fields settled decision 2 requires; every refusal is shown in the database's or engine's own words; no permission decision is made on screen — the buttons are affordances and the database refuses regardless.

Across all eight: backend/engine/ is unmodified (a diff against the package's base proves it); every read and write goes through db.as_person and no privileged connection is introduced; exactly one new migration (0024) exists across the whole package set; full npm run verify is green, including all THREE mutation harnesses (db/test/mutation-check.mjs, engine/mutation_check.py, doorway/mutation_check.py).

No package contains an unresolved decision: WP-003 records the 0024 claim, WP-004 records the parameterless-reads choice, WP-005 records the auditor-cannot-download consequence and the base-tables-not-run_snapshot choice, WP-006 records the storage_uri value and the endpoint-versus-trigger comparison, WP-007 records the api.jsx run-id-parameter rationale.
assumptions: The 'six packages' in plan section 3 is a suggestion ('Suggested work-package cut'), not a constraint, so eight is permitted provided the A->B->C->D order and the E/F placement rules hold.
A migration that only rewrites an RLS policy on cw.run is within WS-1's boundary and does not stray into WS-7's conflict-rule authoring or WS-8's storage decisions.

Hard constraint 2's 'no permission logic in endpoints' governs WHO may act, not WHETHER an act is currently valid; the expiry and validation gates are therefore admissible endpoint logic. If the adjudicator reads it more strictly, WP-006 must instead claim migration 0025 and the package cut is otherwise unchanged.
The engine's run id generation is the doorway's responsibility (the plan says 'generated server-side' and cw.run.run_id has no default), so no engine change is implied.

Screens have no automated rendering test in this repo, so 'tests' for WP-007/WP-008 means shell.test.mjs static assertions plus mutation-check.mjs shell rows plus a recorded manual browser walk — the same bar WP-U07 met.
Synthetic conflict rules seeded as development data are acceptable under the placeholder-content rule and do not require Legal review (plan section 5 item 3, CLAUDE.md, memory.md).
The prototype/v4 screens are the current UI surface (there is no prototype/v4/src); package targets name files under prototype/v4/app/.
unresolved_questions: Is migration 0024 acceptable inside WS-1, or does the owner prefer that the deal-ownership rule be deferred and the gap recorded as a known hole? The plan says both 'no migration is expected' and 'no new migration unless a Part discovers a genuine need'; a Part has discovered one and the two sentences now have to be reconciled by a person.

Should an auditor be able to download a pre-execution contract? Recording document_produced through the caller's connection (which the house pattern demands) means no, because auditors hold no INSERT on cw.audit_event. Nobody has decided this.
What does cw.executed_document.storage_uri carry for an execution filed before WS-8 exists? Settled decision 2 covers hash and signatories and is silent on the column the schema will not let be null.

Should Part B's run reads be parameterless (RLS-scoped, reading-room precedent) or per-run? The recommendation is parameterless, but the plan's endpoint names read as per-run and the choice changes WP-001's scope.

Should the requester gain a new workspace tab for the manifest/run, or should the panes hang off the existing 'my-deals' open-deal view? shell.jsx's tab table is described in its own comment as the specification, so adding a tab is a specification change, not a screen change.
Do the expiry and validation gates belong in the endpoint or in a trigger? WP-006 is instructed to decide and record; the decision itself is not made here.

Does GET /runs/contract download the pre-execution document for an already-executed agreement, or does the executed document supersede it? The plan says pre-execution documents are rebuilt on demand and executed ones are different, but not which one the endpoint answers after execution.

plans.summary: Revision Plan for cutting ASSEMBLY-CONNECTION-PLAN-2026-07-27.md (WS-1) into a Work Package Package. Verified against backend/engine/, backend/doorway/, backend/db/migrations/0004-0009, prototype/v4/. The plan is substantially accurate about the engine and the permission model, but four assertions are contradicted by the repo and several decisions are hidden. Proposed cut: EIGHT packages (WP-001..WP-008) instead of the suggested six, because the bytes-out/parameter transport change is a two-file change (app.py AND server.py) that must own those files alone, and Part E splits at the D boundary the plan itself draws. Tests live inside every package; the three named mutation-harness additions land in WP-005 (rebuild-before-build) and WP-006 (expiry re-check, gate check); the service-level round-trip test lands in WP-005.
information_gathered: Read both plans in full. ASSEMBLY-CONNECTION-PLAN §5 decisions are all SETTLED/CLOSED (lines 225-233), so no open owner questions remain inside WS-1.

Every engine symbol the plan names exists: manifest.py::check_manifest:88, snapshot.py::Snapshot.build:54, resolution.py::resolve:70, validation.py::validate:201 + RuleSet:114, run.py::snapshot_rows:99 / ruleset_rows:144 / run_rows:154 / snapshot_from_rows:262 / SnapshotIncomplete:35, docx.py::build_docx:115.

engine/loader.py does hold live SQL (CLAUSE_SQL:27, RULE_SQL:50, LADDER_SQL:56), so the plan's 'loader.py's queries run over the caller's connection' is correct. Its public entry point is build_snapshot:133, and RULE_SQL selects from cw.active_conflict_rule (not cw.conflict_rule as Part A step 3 says).

0005_run_store.sql: tables snapshot/snapshot_member/snapshot_ladder_rung/ruleset/ruleset_member/run/run_decision/run_finding; views cw.run_snapshot:220, cw.run_contract:231, cw.run_summary:240. cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract are granted to requester/legal_reviewer/legal_admin (line 297) and cw.run_snapshot only to auditor (295). RLS policies read_scoped/write_scoped on run, run_decision, run_finding (271-286).

cw.run requires manifest_source in ('llm','fallback','manual') (0005:88), result_hash ~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ (96), engine_version NOT NULL with NO default (108), gate_open NOT NULL (109), created_by NOT NULL (112). authored_chars/ai_origin_chars were added later by 0009_clause_origin.sql:264-265, so engine/run.py::run_rows' output matches the migrated schema.

cw.run_decision.category_key has an FK to cw.category(key) (0005:138) while the engine speaks category LABELS; engine/run.py::run_rows already does the label->key translation via CategoryMap (run.py:230), and snapshot_from_rows translates back (run.py:339).

0006_executed_agreements.sql: executed_agreement:21 (agreement_id PK -> cw.agreement, run_id nullable FK -> cw.run, executed_on/effective_on NOT NULL), executed_document:60 (byte_size>0, sha256 regex, storage_uri NOT NULL), signature_certificate:312 (certificate bytea NOT NULL, size must match bytes), executed_signatory:332, execution_evidence_gap:355. Insert grants to legal_reviewer/legal_admin only (290, 532); insert policies legal_writes (281-284). Freeze triggers cw.executed_frozen block update/delete/truncate.
cw.agreement status is moved to 'executed' automatically by the trigger executed_agreement_moves_status (0006:206-211); status transitions are policed by a trigger (0006:160-168).

Audit events for both acts are already emitted by triggers: cw.audit_run() fires 'run_recorded' after insert on cw.run (0005:251-263); cw.audit_executed fires 'agreement_executed' (0006:253) and 'document_frozen' (258); signature evidence audits at 391/395.

doorway/reads.py: READS is a dict of parameterless SQL; run(db, caller, key) takes no params (336-348); the reading-room entries carry an explicit doctrine block 'NO PARAMETERS, ON EITHER OF THESE, AND THAT IS THE CONTROL' (276-287).
doorway/writes.py: Write holds exactly one sql string (119-125) and run() executes exactly one statement (495-520). SilentlyRefused converts a zero-row write into a 409 (541-547).

doorway/app.py: Response is frozen with body: dict (48-51); handle() dispatches on the literal 'METHOD /path' key and routes manifests.check as a one-off special case (137-139); there is no query-string parameter anywhere.

doorway/server.py: do_GET passes only parsed.path and drops parsed.query (78-88); _respond unconditionally json.dumps(response.body) and sends application/json (178-185). MAX_BODY is 1,000,000 bytes (56).

doorway/manifests.py: manifest_from:66 is strict about shape, defaults source to 'llm' but accepts any string from the body (line 100); categories_for:105 reads cw.category as the caller; _record:225 writes cw.audit explicitly for both accepted and refused checks, and the long comment at 203-222 is the uniformity argument the plan cites.

doorway/refusals.py: classify() maps OperationalError->500 'broke', SQLSTATE 42501->403 not_permitted, IntegrityError->409 refused_on_merits, RaiseException->409 refused_on_merits, else 400 rejected (70-100). A check-constraint violation therefore surfaces as 409, which is the shape Part A/D refusals need.
doorway/mutation_check.py is a list of (name, file, find, replace, must-fail-test) tuples (55+); MISS and SKIP are both fatal (22-27). It runs only the single named test per mutation.

backend/package.json: 'verify' = test && test:engine && test:doorway && test:mutation; test:mutation runs THREE harnesses - db/test/mutation-check.mjs, engine/mutation_check.py, doorway/mutation_check.py. npm run verify must be invoked from backend/, there is no root package.json.

db/test/mutation-check.mjs does guard UI stub regression (it mutates NotBuiltYet and the workspace pane table at 1173-1976), so the plan's Part E claim is true - but the harness is the JS one, not the doorway one.

db/test/loader-sql.test.mjs extracts CLAUSE_SQL/LADDER_SQL verbatim from loader.py and runs them against the migrated schema; db/test/writer-sql.test.mjs drives run.py's rows into the real schema. These are the existing homes for the plan's 'SQL-against-real-schema' requirement.

prototype/v4/app/ has api.jsx (single API module, no generic get(path)), requester.jsx, reviewer.jsx, workspaces.jsx, library.jsx, common.jsx (NotBuiltYet:97). requester.jsx:315-336 already types a run id by hand and carries the NotBuiltYet 'Intake, the manifest, the forge and the validate findings are not built.'
doorway/writes.py: POST /health-checks/rebuild calls cw.record_rebuild_spot_check(run_id, observed_hash) and compares against cw.run.result_hash (482-487), not against the snapshot id.
memory.md and CLAUDE.md carry the placeholder-content rule (CLAUDE.md:10, memory.md:10) and the two settled WS-1 decisions (memory.md:25, memory.md:40), confirming §5 is closed.
diagnosis: Parts A, C, D map cleanly to bounded single-owner packages. Part B maps cleanly ONLY if it is cut as parameterless policy-scoped reads. Part E does not map to one package. Part F is correctly not a package and should be distributed as the contract requires.

The plan's biggest structural omission is the transport layer. Part B's GET /runs/decisions and GET /runs/findings, and Part C's GET /runs/contract, all imply a per-run selector, but the doorway has no parameter path: reads.run() takes no params, App.handle takes no params, and server.py.do_GET discards the query string. Part C additionally needs bytes out, which requires changing app.py's Response type as well as server.py._respond. app.py and server.py are therefore shared files across A, B, C and E, and need an explicit single owner.

Part A is genuinely over-large for one package and the plan's own A1/A2 suggestion is right, but the split line should be drawn at persistence, not at 'refusing correctly': A1 = manifest re-check + library/rules load as caller + resolve + validate + answer + refusal shapes, no writes at all; A2 = snapshot_rows/ruleset_rows/run_rows persistence, run id generation, agreement linkage, provenance counts, audit reconciliation. A1 has a coherent acceptance test (a run that answers correctly and stores nothing) and A2 has the schema-facing risk.

Hidden decision 1 - audit duplication. cw.run already audits 'run_recorded' by trigger, and cw.executed_agreement already audits 'agreement_executed' by trigger. The endpoints must therefore write only the REFUSAL events explicitly ('run_refused'), and Part A step 6 / Part D step 5 must be restated. Left unresolved, an implementer following the plan literally produces two chain entries per successful run, and the manifests.py uniformity argument silently stops holding because a viewer's refusal path and a requester's success path record through different mechanisms.

Hidden decision 2 - what decides who may call POST /runs. In manifests.py the audit-chain insert grant decides uniformly. For POST /runs, the cw.run write_scoped policy already restricts to requester/legal_reviewer/legal_admin. If the endpoint writes no pre-flight audit row, a viewer submitting a manifest that the engine would refuse never reaches a write and gets an engine-shaped 409 instead of a database refusal - the exact asymmetry manifests.py:203-222 exists to prevent. A package must state which mechanism is authoritative.

Hidden decision 3 - manifest_source. manifests.manifest_from accepts any 'source' string; cw.run.manifest_source is constrained to llm/fallback/manual. The mismatch surfaces as a late 409 IntegrityError rather than a 400 at the boundary. Someone must decide whether manifest_from tightens (a manifests.py change, shared with Part A) or the run endpoint validates.

Hidden decision 4 - the run identifier over the wire. cw.run.run_id has no default and the plan says 'generated server-side'. The generation scheme (uuid? content hash? agreement-scoped sequence?) is unstated and is load-bearing for the round-trip test and for Part C's download URL.

Hidden decision 5 - certificates after filing. memory.md's settled decision says signature certificates are attachable after filing, but cw.signature_certificate has bytea NOT NULL, freeze triggers on update/delete, and no endpoint; and server.py only reads JSON with a 1MB body cap. 'Attachable after' therefore needs its own act (a later insert) and a byte-transport decision. The plan's Part D does not carry it, and WS-8 does not cover it either - it falls between the two.

Sequencing hazard - shared files. Under the plan's six-package suggestion, app.py would be mutated by A, B, C and D; server.py by C; api.jsx by E twice. Without explicit prerequisite edges this violates the contract's no-two-packages-mutate-the-same-file rule. My cut serialises app.py through a declared chain and gives server.py a single owner.

Sequencing hazard - Part E. The plan says 'E can trail B by a package' and 'execution screen after D'. Those are two different prerequisites on two different screens, which is a package boundary, not a note inside one package.

Test placement. The plan puts the round-trip test in Part F prose. It belongs to Part C's package because Part C is where the rebuild happens and where the snapshot-id comparison is performed; the run recording half is already available from A2. Note also that the existing POST /health-checks/rebuild compares result_hash, not snapshot_id - the round-trip test must assert the snapshot id specifically, as the plan says, and should not be conflated with the health check.

Part B is smaller than the plan implies and can be genuinely parameterless: cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract are already policy-scoped through cw.run's read_scoped policy, and cw.run_decision/cw.run_finding policies delegate to cw.run. Selecting them with no WHERE clause returns exactly the caller's rows, which preserves the reading-room doctrine at reads.py:276-287 instead of breaking it.

Content is not a blocker anywhere. The empty conflict-rule catalogue makes validate() a no-op, which A1 must surface as 'rules consulted: 0'. Synthetic seeding is permitted, so a package may seed rules as development data without becoming a content decision.

No migration is needed. Every column, view, grant and policy Parts A-D require exists in 0004-0009. 0024 should stay unclaimed, and every package's acceptance criteria should include 'no migration added'.
symptoms: ASSEMBLY plan Part B calls three new run reads 'the same shape as every existing read', but no existing read takes a parameter and reads.py:276-287 states parameterlessness is a deliberate control.

ASSEMBLY plan Part C says the server change is 'the only change this plan makes outside adding endpoints and screens', but app.py's Response.body is typed dict and server.py drops the query string, so at minimum two files change.
ASSEMBLY plan Part A step 3 says the rule catalogue is loaded from cw.conflict_rule; loader.py RULE_SQL:50 reads cw.active_conflict_rule.
ASSEMBLY plan Part A step 6 and Part D step 5 describe writing run_recorded and agreement_executed from the endpoint; both are already emitted by triggers (0005:254, 0006:253).
ASSEMBLY plan Part F says 'both existing mutation harnesses'; backend/package.json test:mutation runs three.
ASSEMBLY plan Part A step 5 lists what the run row carries but omits engine_version, which is NOT NULL with no default (0005:108).
ASSEMBLY plan Part A step 2 names Snapshot.build as the loader path; the loader's public entry is build_snapshot.
The plan gives no cut for Part E even though its own dependency graph puts one screen after B and another after D.
The plan places the round-trip test in Part F, which is explicitly not a package, leaving the single most important test without an owner.
consequences: If Part A is implemented literally, every successful run produces two 'run_recorded' audit entries - one from the endpoint, one from the trigger - and the audit chain, the one artefact the product is prized for, starts double-counting on day one.

If Part B is started as 'three entries in reads.py' with a run parameter, the implementer either invents a parameter mechanism inside reads.py (breaking the reading-room control that mutation-check.mjs guards) or discovers mid-package that app.py and server.py must change, which is Part C's declared scope - a package collision.
If the transport change is left inside Part C, four packages end up editing app.py with no declared order, and two of them (B and C) can be in flight simultaneously under the plan's own graph.

If manifest_source is not reconciled, a manifest with source 'human' or 'v3' passes the trust boundary, resolves, builds a snapshot, and then fails at INSERT with a check-constraint 409 - work discarded and a refusal that names a column rather than the caller's mistake.

If the certificate-after-filing act is not owned, decision 2 in memory.md is recorded as settled but unimplementable: there is no endpoint, no byte transport, and the freeze triggers make a later UPDATE impossible.
If the round-trip test is not assigned, the most load-bearing guarantee in WS-1 ships untested, and the existing POST /health-checks/rebuild (which compares result_hash) reads as though it covers it.
If Part E is one package, the requester screens cannot ship until D lands, delaying the reading-room and pipeline-rail payoff the plan names as WS-1's main unblock.
proposed_actions: Cut WS-1 into EIGHT single-owner packages, WP-001..WP-008, IDs stable and never renumbered. risks: Widening app.py's Response to carry bytes is the single riskiest change in the set: every existing endpoint returns through it, and a careless branch could serialise a dict as bytes or leak a stack trace through the new path. Mitigated by giving WP-004 sole ownership, no new endpoint, and its own mutation rows.

Introducing any parameter into the doorway risks eroding the reading-room control that mutation-check.mjs guards. Mitigated by making WP-003 strictly parameterless and confining the selector in WP-004 to a whitelisted single value used only by GET /runs/contract.

POST /runs is a long transaction with many inserts through a role-bound connection; db.py's Request exposes no executemany, so the insert loop is hand-written and a partial failure must roll the whole run back. A half-written run is worse than no run.

The round-trip test needs a genuinely non-trivial seeded library (clauses, ladders with a floor, at least one conflict rule) or it will pass vacuously on an empty snapshot. Synthetic seeding is allowed, but the package must assert non-emptiness rather than assume it.

Adding rows to doorway/mutation_check.py is fragile by construction: the find string must match the source verbatim, and MISS and SKIP are both fatal. A refactor inside the same package can turn its own new mutation into a stale SKIP and redden the bar.

Part D touches frozen tables with triggers that raise. Every refusal path must be exercised as a real role against the migrated schema; a mocked test here proves nothing (the trap named in handoff 07 §5.2 and honoured by writer-sql.test.mjs).

The suite rebuilds the schema per test and the doorway suite is already slow; eight packages each adding endpoint tests will lengthen npm run verify materially. Worth stating as an accepted cost rather than discovering it.

Eight packages exceed the plan's suggested six. If the reviewing owner treats six as binding, WP-004 would fold into WP-005 and WP-008 into WP-007 - at the cost of two packages each owning a file another package also needs.

No two packages mutate the same file without a declared prerequisite edge between them; app.py's writers are ordered WP-001, WP-004, WP-005, WP-006 and server.py has exactly one writer (WP-004).

WP-001 acceptance: a requester submitting a manifest with a category the library does not define is refused with check_manifest's own sentence at 409; a viewer is refused by the database before any engine answer is reported; an empty conflict-rule catalogue is reported as zero rules consulted, not as a passing validation; a rungless ladder or unbuildable snapshot refuses loudly with the engine's own error; nothing is written to cw.run.

WP-002 acceptance: a recorded run appears in cw.run with a non-null engine_version and a valid result_hash; the audit chain contains exactly ONE 'run_recorded' entry per successful run; a refused run produces a 'run_refused' entry and no cw.run row; the statements are exercised against the migrated schema in writer-sql.test.mjs; a run cannot be recorded without a deal reference.

[BOTH · RT1-EV-119 · Observed] cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member and cw.snapshot_ladder_rung have NO row-level security at all — 0005:266-268 enables RLS on run, run_decision and run_finding only — while SELECT is granted to all three writing roles (0005:288). planner-A WP-005 explicitly directs Part C to rebuild from these base tables (correctly, given the run_snapshot grant), which means any requester holding a snapshot_id can rebuild a pinned library another deal used. A DROP+CREATE in a migration that another migration later re-runs, or a rename mismatch against 0013's administrator_reads on the same table, fails closed in a confusing way — A's own risk text anticipates the symptom without naming the statement.

[BOTH · RT1-EV-121 · Observed] Both packages route Part D's expiry gate through per-clause state without noting that cw.run_drift, the one view that already does the pinned-version join, is itself scoped by cw.app_role() in its WHERE clause (0022:198-200) and is a VIEW over person-scoped cw.run/cw.agreement — i.e. correct here precisely because 0022's author remembered the owner-rights rule.
