recommended_corrections: Adjudicate the Part B read source on the evidence, not on the plan's prose: either scope cw.run_summary / cw.run_contract in a new migration the way 0017 and 0019 scoped their views (WHERE clause repeating the policy, since security_invoker is the wrong tool here for the same reason 0017 records), or have the run reads select from the base tables cw.run, cw.run_decision and cw.run_finding, which do carry RLS. Whichever is chosen, add both views to backend/db/test/views-are-not-policies.test.mjs's REVIEWED inventory with a verdict, and extend that test's catalogue query beyond cw_viewer so requester-readable views are covered — the guard that would have caught this does not look where the leak is.

Settle the deal-binding fact once, in the integrated package set, in these words: cw.run's INSERT policy is role-only (0005:276-277) and no migration in 0001-0023 constrains agreement_id on insert. Then choose explicitly — claim 0024 with the two-branch policy shape used everywhere else (`cw.app_role() in ('legal_reviewer','legal_admin') or (cw.app_role() = 'requester' and cw.owns_agreement(agreement_id))`, plus a decision about whether agreement_id becomes NOT NULL), or record the hole as a carried gap with an owner. Do not merge planner-A's literal policy text; it locks Legal out of recording runs.

Delete 'Audit agreement_executed' from planner-A's WP-006 required changes and its acceptance, replacing it with planner-B's formulation: the endpoint writes only refusal events; cw.audit_executed (0006:249-266) owns the success event, exactly as cw.audit_run (0005:251-263) owns run_recorded. Both packages should assert 'exactly one agreement_executed per execution' rather than 'agreement_executed is recorded'.

Move the 'GET /reading-room/clauses returns rows' acceptance criterion out of the Part B package into the execution package, and state its real precondition: an executed agreement whose run_id is set, plus a live cw.agreement_share row for the viewer (0017:186-222). Keep WP-U15's 'do not fake the run' instruction attached to it.

Correct planner-A's WP-005: the value fed to POST /health-checks/rebuild is the run's recomputed result_hash, not the .docx sha256 (writes.py:487-490; resolution.py:87). The document digest belongs in the document_produced audit payload only. State the two hashes side by side in the package so no implementer conflates them.

Add an idempotency clause to whichever package persists a run: insert cw.snapshot / cw.snapshot_member / cw.snapshot_ladder_rung / cw.ruleset / cw.ruleset_member only when the content-addressed id is absent, citing backend/db/test/writer-sql.test.mjs:125-137 ('a real writer inserts them if absent'), and add a named test that records two runs against an unchanged library and expects one snapshot row and two run rows.

Record the provenance-count decision explicitly: cw.run is immutable and has no UPDATE grant (0005:188-214, 288-290), so authored_chars / ai_origin_chars are whatever POST /runs wrote and the plan's Part C sentence 'the counts land on the run record' cannot be implemented. Either the run endpoint builds the document to count, or the counts stay zero and the packages say so.

Repair planner-B's dependency graph: give the requester download its own edge (WP-004 transport -> WP-005 document -> WP-007 screens) instead of the self-referential '{WP-005, WP-007} -> WP-007 download half', or split the download screen into its own package. Reconcile planner-A's graph with its WP-007 text (WP-005 is a prerequisite of the download half either way).

Fix the cited-fact errors before the packages are issued, since implementers will use them as anchors: audit-chain INSERT also belongs to cw_administrator (0013:257); reads.py holds 29 parameterless Read entries, not 24; the requester NotBuiltYet is at prototype/v4/app/requester.jsx:343; loader-sql.test.mjs already extracts RULE_SQL; cw.executed_document.kind must appear in the execution insert set.

Weaken planner-A's WP-001 mutation row or defer it: a query parameter that nothing consumes cannot be guarded by a named failing test under doorway/mutation_check.py's rules (MISS and SKIP both fatal). Either ship the transport package together with its first consumer's test, or state the mutation as the bytes-path one planner-B proposes, which is observable.
blocking_issues: Both plans instruct Part B's run reads to select from cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract while asserting the database scopes them. Those views bypass RLS by owner-rights and carry no WHERE clause of their own (0005:220-248, 297; 0017:160-186; views-are-not-policies.test.mjs). Integrating either package set as written ships a cross-requester run leak and a false acceptance criterion.

The two plans give opposite answers on the load-bearing schema fact — planner-A says cw.run's INSERT policy has no ownership condition and claims migration 0024; planner-B says RLS already decides ownership and forbids a migration. The repo supports planner-A's fact (0005:276-277) and refutes planner-B's instruction, but planner-A's proposed policy text would refuse legal_reviewer and legal_admin (cw.owns_agreement is actor-based, 0003:626-631). Neither version can be merged as written; the deal-binding rule must be adjudicated and rewritten before any package is issued.

Planner-A's WP-006 instructs an endpoint-side agreement_executed audit that the schema's own trigger already emits (0006:249-266), producing two irreconcilable entries in a chain with no UPDATE or DELETE grant. This is the exact failure planner-A itself identified for run_recorded.

Neither plan specifies idempotent insertion of content-addressed snapshot/ruleset rows, so the second run against an unchanged library fails with a unique-violation surfaced as a 409 refusal (0005:66-76; writer-sql.test.mjs:125-137 shows the repo already solved this in test).

reviews.review_lens: Architecture and Risk Auditor — package boundaries, shared-file collisions and sequencing, hidden design decisions inside packages, engine-untouched rule, permission logic sneaking into endpoints, the server.py bytes-out change scoped bigger than one thin addition, scope drift into WS-2/4/6/7/8
major_defects: BOTH planners (blocking, shared): Part B is designed to read cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract as parameterless, 'policy-scoped' reads. Verified false. Neither view carries a WHERE clause (backend/db/migrations/0005_run_store.sql:231-249), neither is declared security_invoker (no occurrence anywhere in migrations), and both are granted to cw_requester/cw_legal_reviewer/cw_legal_admin (0005:296-298). This repo has already paid for this exact bug three times and documents the rule in its own words at 0017_reading_room.sql:165-200 ('a view runs with its owner's rights and does NOT inherit the policies underneath it') and again at 0022:196-199. cw.run's read_scoped policy (0005:271-275) is therefore never consulted through those views. A parameterless SELECT from cw.run_summary hands every requester every run in the system — vendor, agreement_id, result_hash, created_by — and cw.run_contract hands over every clause of every deal's contract. The correct source is the RLS-bearing base tables cw.run / cw.run_decision / cw.run_finding (granted at 0005:288-290, RLS enabled at 0005:266-268), or scoped views written the way cw.run_drift (0022:198-200) and cw.reading_room (0017:196-200) are written.

BOTH planners (blocking, shared): the existing guard will not catch the leak above. backend/db/test/views-are-not-policies.test.mjs enumerates only views on which cw_viewer holds SELECT (its catalogue query filters has_table_privilege('cw_viewer', ...)). cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract are not granted to cw_viewer, so they fall outside the inventory. Both package sets treat 'npm run verify green' as sufficient evidence that the reads are scoped; it is not, for precisely these two views.

planner-B (major): WP-002's stated design is 'require an agreement reference and let cw.run's RLS decide ownership', and its acceptance criterion is 'a run cannot be recorded without a deal reference'. cw.run's INSERT policy is write_scoped ... with check (cw.app_role() in ('requester','legal_reviewer','legal_admin')) — role only, no ownership term (0005:276-277), in deliberate contrast with the SELECT policy three lines above which does call cw.owns_agreement. Nothing in the database stops requester X recording a run against requester Y's agreement_id, and the audit trigger (0005:251-266) will record it as legitimate with no correction possible (no UPDATE/DELETE grant on cw.audit_event, 0001:339-346). B's EV-216 ('cw.run's RLS policies already scope reads by role and ownership') is tagged Observed but conflates the read policy with the write policy; B's EV-233 ('no migration is required') rests on that conflation. planner-A's EV-103 is correct and B's is not. The 'no deal reference' half is also endpoint-side gatekeeping standing in for a database rule, which is the shape hard constraint 2 exists to prevent.

planner-B (major): WP-001's acceptance criterion 'a viewer is refused by the database before any engine answer is reported' cannot be met inside WP-001's own declared scope. WP-001 explicitly writes nothing ('nothing is written to cw.run', no audit row), and a viewer holds SELECT on cw.clause_version (0002:354), the ladder tables (0003:670) and cw.active_conflict_rule (0004:238). With no write anywhere in the transaction the database has no occasion to refuse: a viewer gets a full engine answer or an engine-shaped refusal. B identifies this as 'hidden decision 2' and then defers it to WP-002, which means WP-001 is approved with a known violation of the manifests.py uniformity rule (manifests.py:203-222) and an acceptance criterion that will be signed off on a test that cannot honestly pass. planner-A's WP-002 avoids this by writing the attempt row first (cw.audit is language sql, not SECURITY DEFINER, 0001:328-336, so a viewer's INSERT is refused at the boundary).

BOTH planners (major, shared): the server.py bytes-out change is scoped well past the contract's 'one thin addition' on an unexamined premise. Both assume a run selector must travel in the URL, and both therefore change _endpoint()/do_GET to stop discarding the query string (planner-A WP-001(b); planner-B WP-004 'pass parsed.query through App.handle'). The doorway already names a run without any transport change: POST /health-checks/rebuild takes run_id and observed_hash from the request body via Write.fields (writes.py:487-489, bind() at writes.py:126-146), and POST /health-checks/document takes agreement_id and doc_seq the same way. GET vs POST for /runs/contract is a Part C detail of the plan, not a section-5 settled decision. Neither planner records the body-carried-selector alternative or the reason for rejecting it, so the riskiest file in the service (every endpoint passes through _respond) is opened for a reason that was never tested. planner-A compounds it by putting that change at WP-001, the head of the entire critical path.

planner-B (major): unresolved decisions are left inside packages that are nonetheless proposed for approval, against the success criterion 'no hidden unresolved decisions'. B's own unresolved list carries the run-id generation scheme (WP-002 'must fix it', but no answer given), query parameter vs path segment (recommended, not decided, and it sets WP-004's scope), where manifest_source reconciliation lives (manifests.py vs runs.py — B notes both endpoints can disagree about what a valid manifest is and then does not choose), and what storage_uri carries pre-WS-8 (NOT NULL at 0006:72, no value proposed). planner-A resolves the equivalent items inside the owning packages and routes only genuinely owner-level questions upward.
minor_defects: planner-A: WP-002's prerequisite is hedged — 'Prerequisites: WP-001 (none strictly, but sequenced to keep app.py single-owner)'. app.py is written by WP-001, WP-002, WP-005 and WP-006; the no-concurrent-mutation guarantee rests entirely on that edge being hard. A hedged prerequisite is not an edge.

planner-A: the dependency line 'WP-004 -> {WP-005 -> WP-006, WP-007}' places WP-007 parallel to WP-005, but the WP-007 entry says 'WP-004 for the run view and WP-005 for the download'. The graph and the package text disagree about whether the download half of the requester screen is gated on Part C.

planner-A: WP-002 is described as 'NO persistence, no run id' while it writes run_attempted/run_refused rows into cw.audit_event, which has no UPDATE or DELETE grant for any role (0001:339-346). The event vocabulary chosen in WP-002 is permanent before WP-003 has finished deciding what a recorded run looks like, and successful A1 runs will leave attempt rows with no run behind them.

planner-B: the prerequisite graph contains the malformed edge '{WP-005, WP-007} -> WP-007 download half' — WP-007 appears on both sides of its own edge — and WP-007 is separately given prerequisite WP-003 in the main chain. WP-007 owns five files (api.jsx, requester.jsx, workspaces.jsx, shell.test.mjs, mutation-check.mjs); its start condition must be unambiguous.

planner-B: WP-001, WP-002 and WP-005 each own a 'half' of backend/doorway/runs.py, and WP-004 owns 'app.py's Response type' while WP-001/005/006 add routes to the same file. Sub-file ownership is weaker than the contract's file-level rule; it happens to be linearly ordered here, but it should be stated as file ownership with an ordering, not as regions.

planner-B: escalating 'signature certificates attachable after filing' to a blocker on WP-006 approval overstates it. Settled decision 2 requires hash and signatories AT FILING and explicitly makes the certificate a later attachment; cw.signature_certificate has its own INSERT grant (0006:532) and its own table, so a later insert is possible — what is missing is byte transport, which is genuinely a later workstream, not a WS-1 approval gate. B's underlying observation (JSON-only server, 1MB cap at server.py:56) is correct and is worth carrying as a named follow-on, not as a blocker.

planner-A: WP-006 is told to use cw.run_drift for the expiry gate. cw.run_drift inner-joins cw.agreement and filters a.status <> 'executed' (0022:174-192), and cw.executed_agreement's insert trigger moves status to executed (0006:206-211). The gate must be evaluated before the executed_agreement insert in the same transaction, or the view stops returning rows for the run being executed. A does not name the ordering. (The view is granted to reviewer and admin at 0022:210-211, so the source itself is viable.)
unsupported_claims: planner-B EV-216 (tagged Observed): 'cw.run's RLS policies already scope reads by role and ownership, and run_decision/run_finding delegate to cw.run, which makes a parameterless Part B genuinely correct rather than a compromise.' The policy text is quoted correctly; the conclusion does not follow, because the reads B specifies go through cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract, which bypass those policies. Mis-tagged: the inference is Assumed, and it is wrong.

planner-B EV-233 (tagged Inferred): 'No migration is required for Parts A-D; every table, view, grant and policy already exists.' Every object exists; the ownership CONDITION on cw.run's INSERT does not. The claim is true about objects and false about the rule the settled deal-binding decision needs.

planner-A WP-004 and planner-B WP-003 both assert the run reads are 'scoped by the database' with no supporting evidence item about view semantics. Neither planner produced an EV item for the one fact that decides it, despite both having read 0005 in full and despite the repo carrying a dedicated test file about this failure class.

planner-A: 'Part C cannot be a single bounded change to server.py as the plan claims... Both the bytes-out change and a routing/parameter change land in server.py and app.py.' The premise (no path/query parameters) is Observed and correct; the necessity claim is Assumed and is disconfirmed by writes.py's existing body-carried run_id.

planner-B: 'the freeze triggers make a later UPDATE impossible' offered as evidence that certificate-after-filing is unimplementable. The freeze triggers are on update/delete/truncate (0006:118-123, 378-383); the act is an INSERT into a separate table that has its own grant. The obstacle is byte transport only.
missed_risks: planner-B missed entirely: recording 'document_produced' through the caller's own connection denies the Part C download to auditors and viewers, because INSERT on cw.audit_event is granted only to requester, legal_reviewer and legal_admin (0001:339-346) while cw.run's read policy admits auditors (0005:271-273). planner-A caught this (EV-107/EV-108) and correctly classifies it as a decision that must be recorded rather than discovered. B's WP-005 writes the event and B's WP-003 acceptance assumes auditors read runs, so B ships the contradiction unnoticed.

BOTH: cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member, cw.snapshot_ladder_rung and cw.ruleset carry NO row-level security at all — only cw.run, cw.run_decision and cw.run_finding get it (0005:265-268). Both planners correctly route Part C's rebuild to the base snapshot tables (because cw.run_snapshot is auditor-only, 0005:293-295), but neither states that the snapshot tables therefore provide no scoping of their own: the entire protection for 'whose document is this' is the cw.run row lookup that names the snapshot_id. If that lookup goes through cw.run_summary, the leak in the first blocking issue becomes a cross-tenant document download, not just a cross-tenant list.

BOTH: neither package set requires the new run reads to be added to the views-are-not-policies inventory or to extend that harness beyond viewer-readable views, so the next unscoped view over person-scoped data lands with the same silence as the last three.

BOTH: no package carries a rollback note for a migration or for the transport change, despite the contract naming rollback notes as a per-package requirement. planner-A names 0024 risks (policy drop/recreate leaving cw.run momentarily without a write policy) but stops short of a rollback procedure; planner-B has no migration and no rollback statement for the Response-type widening either.

planner-A: migration 0024 rewrites write_scoped on cw.run, a table that also carries immutability triggers and an administrator_reads policy from a later migration. A names the risk but the acceptance criteria do not require asserting that the OTHER policies on cw.run are unchanged after 0024 runs.
recommended_corrections: Before any package is issued, settle the run-read source in writing: the Part B reads select from cw.run, cw.run_decision and cw.run_finding (RLS-bearing tables, already granted at 0005:288-290), or from new views that repeat the policy in their own WHERE clause in the style of cw.run_drift (0022:198-200). Do not select from cw.run_summary or cw.run_contract as they stand. Whichever is chosen, the owning package's acceptance criteria must include the per-role assertion planner-A already wrote ('an auditor sees every run, a requester sees only runs they created or runs on their own deals, a viewer is refused') executed against the migrated schema, and must add the new views to backend/db/test/views-are-not-policies.test.mjs with their verdict word, extending that file's catalogue query beyond cw_viewer.

Adjudicate the cw.run INSERT-ownership gap explicitly, in favour of planner-A's reading: the settled decision 'runs are tied to deals' has no database rule behind it (0005:276-277), hard constraint 2 forbids fixing it in the endpoint, and hard constraint 4 permits a package to claim 0024 with a recorded reason. Either approve planner-A's WP-003 migration 0024 (with run-store tests asserting both directions for all three writing roles) or record the hole as an accepted, named risk — but do not adopt planner-B's WP-002 wording, which asserts an enforcement that does not exist.

Re-scope the transport work to the smallest change that satisfies Part C. Require the integrated package set to record, as a decision, why the run selector travels where it does — and to consider the existing precedent (run_id in the POST body, writes.py:487-489) before touching _endpoint()/do_GET. If the body-carried selector is adopted, server.py's change collapses to the single bytes-out branch the contract anticipates, app.py's Response gains one variant, and Part B needs no transport predecessor at all, which removes planner-A's WP-001 from the head of the critical path.

Adopt planner-A's audit reconciliation verbatim in whichever cut is integrated: the endpoints write only the attempt/refusal events (run_attempted / run_refused), never run_recorded or agreement_executed, both of which are already emitted by triggers (0005:251-266, 0006:249-268). Make 'exactly one run_recorded per run' and 'exactly one agreement_executed per execution' named acceptance assertions.

Fix planner-B's WP-001 boundary: either A1 writes the attempt row (making the database the thing that refuses a viewer, as planner-A does) or WP-001's viewer acceptance criterion is struck and the uniformity gap is carried explicitly to WP-002. Do not ship the criterion as written.

Make every prerequisite an unconditional edge. Strike planner-A's 'none strictly, but sequenced' on WP-002, resolve A's WP-007 graph-vs-text disagreement about the download half, and replace planner-B's self-referential '{WP-005, WP-007} -> WP-007 download half' with two ordinary edges. Re-express planner-B's sub-file ownership (halves of runs.py, 'app.py's Response type') as whole-file ownership plus an ordering.

Force the deferred decisions in planner-B's list to be answered inside the owning packages before approval: run-id generation scheme, storage_uri's pre-WS-8 value and its shape, and whether manifest_source is tightened in manifests.manifest_from (a visible behaviour change to the live POST /manifests/check) or validated in the run endpoint. Leaving the last one open guarantees the two endpoints disagree about what a valid manifest is.

Carry certificate-after-filing as a named follow-on with an owner, not as a WP-006 approval blocker: settled decision 2 requires hash and signatories at filing only, cw.signature_certificate has its own INSERT grant (0006:532), and the missing piece is byte transport past a JSON-only, 1MB-capped server (server.py:56).

Add the ordering constraint planner-A's WP-006 lacks: if the expiry gate reads cw.run_drift, it must be evaluated before the cw.executed_agreement insert, because that insert's trigger moves the agreement to 'executed' (0006:206-211) and the view filters status <> 'executed' (0022:192).

Require every package to carry an explicit rollback note (the contract asks for one and neither planner supplies them), and require the 0024-claiming package, if approved, to assert that cw.run's other policies survive the rewrite.
blocking_issues: Both package sets design Part B (and, downstream, Part C's run lookup) on cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract, which bypass cw.run's row-level security because a PostgreSQL view runs with its owner's rights and these two carry no WHERE clause of their own and are not security_invoker (0005:231-249, 296-298; the rule is written out in this repo at 0017:165-200 and 0022:196-199). Implementing either cut as written turns the first real runs into a cross-tenant disclosure of every deal's runs and every deal's contract clauses to every requester — and the existing views-are-not-policies harness will not catch it, because its inventory is limited to viewer-readable views. This must be corrected before any package is issued.

planner-B asserts, as the enforcement mechanism for the SETTLED 'runs are tied to deals' decision, that cw.run's RLS decides ownership on insert. It does not (0005:276-277 checks role only, deliberately unlike the SELECT policy directly above it). Integrating B's WP-002 as written ships POST /runs with no rule preventing a requester from attaching a run to another requester's deal, permanently recorded as legitimate by the audit trigger. Either adopt planner-A's 0024 or record the hole as accepted; do not integrate the false claim.

reviews.review_lens: Testing and Completion Auditor — testability of acceptance criteria, named tests, placement of the service-level round trip, assignment and writability of the three mandated mutation-harness additions, refusal-by-database coverage per role, and npm run verify preserved as each package's closing check. All claims verified against repo ground truth (read-only).
major_defects: BOTH (planner-A, planner-B) — Mutation rows are unwritable as specified. Observed (EV-RT3-101): backend/doorway/mutation_check.py rows are 5-tuples whose fifth element is a literal pytest node id (e.g. lines 62, 176, 233: 'test_reads.py::test_a_refusal_never_arrives_as_an_empty_list'), and the header states MISS and SKIP are BOTH fatal. Neither planner supplies the node id for any of the three mandated additions ('break the expiry re-check', 'break the gate check', 'break the rebuild-before-build'), nor the verbatim find/replace strings. Both plans reduce to 'caught by the test that names it', which is circular: the row cannot be authored, and the contract's requirement that each addition be CAUGHT cannot be evaluated at acceptance.

BOTH (planner-A WP-005, planner-B WP-005) — The most load-bearing negative test on the first parameterised endpoint is missing. Observed (EV-RT3-102): 0005_run_store.sql:266-268 enables row-level security on cw.run, cw.run_decision and cw.run_finding ONLY. cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member, cw.snapshot_ladder_rung, cw.ruleset and cw.ruleset_member have NO RLS and are granted select to cw_requester, cw_legal_reviewer, cw_legal_admin (0005:288-291) and cw_auditor (0005:292-295). Both planners correctly route GET /runs/contract to those base tables — but neither names a test that a caller supplying ANOTHER caller's run id (or snapshot id) is refused, and neither names the corollary test that zero rows from the RLS-scoped cw.run lookup must surface as a refusal rather than an empty or partial document. As specified, the download's only scoping is the endpoint's own run_id->cw.run resolution, which is untested in both cuts and sits directly against hard constraint 2.

BOTH (planner-A WP-004, planner-B WP-003) — Part B ships the bar red. Observed (EV-RT3-103): backend/doorway/test_reads.py:92-101 contains test_the_read_count_moves_only_on_purpose asserting len(READS) == 29 with the message '25 ported plus 4 added on purpose'. Both planners add three or four READS entries in the Part B package; neither lists that assertion among the required changes, and neither package's acceptance criteria mention it. npm run verify cannot be green at the close of Part B in either cut.

planner-B (WP-001) — The package's headline refusal criterion is unachievable inside the package. B scopes WP-001 as 'no writes at all' yet its acceptance requires 'a viewer is refused by the database before any engine answer is reported'. Observed (EV-RT3-104): cw_viewer holds select on cw.clause_version_state and cw.selectable_clause (0002_clause_registry.sql:352-354), on cw.active_conflict_rule (0004:237-238), and on cw.ladder, cw.ladder_rung, cw.ladder_rung_state and cw.ladder_health (0003:669-670). A write-free POST /runs therefore refuses nobody — a viewer would receive the engine's complete answer. B itself defers the question to WP-002 ('hidden decision 2'), leaving WP-001's acceptance criterion unsatisfiable. planner-A avoids this by having WP-002 write a run_attempted audit row first, where the audit-insert grant (0001:339-346) does the refusing.

planner-B (WP-006) — The 'break the expiry re-check' mutation has no writable test. B specifies the expiry gate and its acceptance against 'cw.clause_version_state's expiry columns'. Observed (EV-RT3-105): expiry is computed as v.expires_on < current_date (0002:241, 0009:70), and cw.clause_version.expires_on is IMMUTABLE — 0002:126-155 cw.clause_version_immutable() raises restrict_violation on any change to expires_on, and the trigger clause_version_no_edit fires before update. An already-expired version is not selectable (0002:256) and so is never pinned by a run. A date-based lapse between run and signature therefore cannot be induced in a test, so no test can be authored for the gate, so the mandated mutation row is unwritable. planner-A partially escapes by naming cw.run_drift (0022:173-200), which also keys off supersession and retirement — the only inducible paths.

planner-A — npm run verify is not preserved as the closing check of EACH package. It appears only once, as a set-level criterion ('Across all eight: ... full npm run verify is green, including all THREE mutation harnesses'). The objective contract requires the full verify to stay green per package, and A's per-package acceptance blocks name only local tests. planner-B states it correctly as a per-package definition of done.

planner-A (WP-004) — Violates 'F lives inside every package'. WP-004's target files include prototype/v4/app/api.jsx ('read functions only, no panes'), but its test surface is backend/doorway/test_reads.py alone; backend/db/test/shell.test.mjs and backend/db/test/mutation-check.mjs — the only files that assert anything about api.jsx (shell.test.mjs:234-269, 541-544, 957-990) — are assigned to WP-007. The api.jsx change therefore ships with no test in its own package.

planner-B — The dependency graph is ill-formed and cannot be executed as written: '{WP-005, WP-007} -> WP-007 download half' makes WP-007 its own prerequisite, and 'WP-007 download half' concedes WP-007 is two packages. The single-writer ordering for prototype/v4/app/api.jsx is therefore unresolved, which is exactly the collision the eight-package cut was chosen to prevent.
minor_defects: BOTH — Refusal-by-database coverage is exemplar-only, not per role. The plan's Part F requires 'every role that must be refused is refused BY THE DATABASE'. planner-A names one role per endpoint (viewer on POST /runs, requester on POST /agreements/execute); planner-B likewise. Auditor and viewer on POST /agreements/execute, viewer and auditor on GET /runs/contract, and the positive legal_reviewer/legal_admin cases are unnamed in both. Observed (EV-RT3-106): the existing parametrised sweeps in test_reads.py:153-166 cover only administrator and requester, so the missing role coverage is NOT inherited from the harness.

BOTH — Neither package set names the fixture mechanism that makes a pinned clause version lapse between run and execution. Per EV-RT3-105 the only inducible paths are inserting a cw.supersession row with predecessor_disposition='retire_now' (0002:194-211) or setting cw.clause_version.retired = true. Without naming one, the expiry-gate test and its mutation are left to the implementer to invent mid-package.

BOTH — The new download mechanism erodes an existing guard that neither planner extends. Observed (EV-RT3-107): shell.test.mjs's 'the viewer has no export path of any kind' (lines 974-991) checks only viewer.jsx source for createElement('a'), URL.createObjectURL, new Blob(, .download and window.print. Once a docx download helper exists in api.jsx (WP-007 in both cuts), nothing asserts it stays off the viewer's surface. Neither planner names extending that assertion to api.jsx or to the viewer pane's call list.

planner-A — Mutation-harness semantics are stated backwards: 'each must be seen to go from ok to MISS when removed'. Observed (EV-RT3-101): a row reports 'ok' when the named test FAILS under mutation; deleting the guarded code makes the find string absent and the row reports SKIP (stale), not MISS. An implementer following this wording can author a row that goes silently stale.

planner-A (WP-004) — 'and optionally GET /runs/drift' is a hidden unresolved decision inside a package (contract: no hidden unresolved decisions) and makes the required READS-count edit (EV-RT3-103) unspecifiable: 32 or 33.

planner-A (WP-005) — The round trip carries no non-vacuity assertion. planner-B's EV-234 correctly flags that the round trip passes trivially against a thin snapshot; A's WP-005 acceptance asserts only that the ids match. A's seeding instruction lives in WP-002/WP-003 and is not bound to the round-trip criterion.

planner-A (WP-005) — 'build_docx's zero-authored-characters assertion holds and no provenance footer appears on the document' is stated as an outcome with no named test and no file; it is the engine's own invariant restated rather than a doorway acceptance check.

planner-B — Omits the observation that the screens have no rendering test: shell.test.mjs is static analysis over source. B's WP-007/WP-008 acceptance ('no pane fetches broadly and filters on screen', 'every call maps to one role-scoped endpoint') therefore reads as automated coverage it does not have. planner-A states this honestly and requires a recorded browser walk.
planner-A — The recorded browser walk in WP-007/WP-008 has no pass/fail definition and is not reachable by npm run verify; as written it is an acceptance criterion no reviewer can score.

planner-B (WP-003) — 'GET /reading-room/clauses returns rows once a real run exists behind an agreement, with no further code' is asserted without evidence. The reading-room reads are share-scoped (test_reads.py:331-346, shell.test.mjs:951-971); nothing shown demonstrates that recording a run alone populates them.
unsupported_claims: planner-B, EV-233: 'No migration is required for Parts A-D; every table, view, grant and policy already exists in 0004-0009, so 0024 should remain unclaimed.' Disconfirmed. Observed (EV-RT3-108): 0005_run_store.sql:276-277 — create policy write_scoped on cw.run for insert with check (cw.app_role() in ('requester','legal_reviewer','legal_admin')) — carries NO agreement-ownership condition, in contrast to the SELECT policy at 0005:271-275 which does call cw.owns_agreement. planner-A's EV-103 is correct on this point and planner-B's EV-233 is not.

planner-B, WP-002: 'require an agreement reference and let cw.run's RLS decide ownership', with the acceptance criterion 'a run cannot be recorded without a deal reference'. Per EV-RT3-108 the database will not decide ownership, so this criterion is only satisfiable by an endpoint-side check — i.e. by permission logic in an endpoint, which hard constraint 2 forbids. From this lens the defect is that the criterion cannot be tested as a database refusal at all, yet is written as one.

planner-B, WP-004 acceptance: 'a mutation that makes the bytes path serialise as JSON is caught by the one test that names it.' No such test exists today (backend/doorway/test_server.py contains no bytes-path test) and B names neither the test nor the row. The criterion asserts a guard that the package is also responsible for creating.

planner-A, WP-001 acceptance: 'one mutation row proves the JSON path is still guarded.' Which guarantee, which find string and which named test are all unspecified — the same unwritability as the three mandated rows.

BOTH — 'refusals classified by refusals.py house pattern' is carried as a shared assumption without a named test proving classification for the NEW failure modes (a 42501 from an unscoped base-table read, an engine RaiseException on an id mismatch). refusals.py needing no change is plausible but is asserted, not evidenced by a test either package owns.
missed_risks: Confirmed by both cuts' silence: cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member, cw.snapshot_ladder_rung, cw.ruleset and cw.ruleset_member carry NO row-level security (0005:266-268 enables it on run/run_decision/run_finding only) while being granted to four roles. Both planners direct WP-005 to read exactly these tables and neither treats the absence of RLS as a risk. The document endpoint is the first place a caller-supplied identifier reaches an unscoped table, and the audit chain will record the resulting download as legitimate.

cw.run_drift (planner-A's recommended source for the Part D expiry gate) is documented as REPORTING ONLY — 0022:203-208: 'REPORTING ONLY: nothing here changes a run or a contract'. It also INNER JOINs cw.agreement and filters where a.status <> 'executed'. A run with a null agreement_id is invisible to the view, so an expiry gate built on it passes silently for any such run. Neither planner names a test for the null-agreement case, and planner-A does not reconcile the gate's use with the view's stated reporting-only contract.

The mutation harness's own fragility under this workload is understated. Observed: doorway/mutation_check.py currently holds 24 rows and its header records that the doorway suite rebuilds the schema per test and takes about four minutes. Both cuts add three rows plus several new test modules; planner-B flags the SKIP-staleness risk, planner-A flags the runtime, and neither proposes a check that the new rows are re-run after any in-package refactor of the file they mutate.

Neither cut names a test for the ordering guarantee the whole engagement rests on: that the rebuild happens BEFORE the bytes are built. The mutation row is named in both, but no acceptance criterion states the observable — that a run which fails to reproduce produces NO bytes at all rather than bytes plus a warning.

Neither cut names a negative test for the audit half of the document act: that when the audit insert is refused (auditor, viewer — 0001:339-346), the transaction rolls back and no bytes are returned. planner-A records the consequence as a decision but not as a test.
recommended_corrections: Require every package that adds a mutation to state the row VERBATIM as the 5-tuple doorway/mutation_check.py expects — (name, file, find, replace, 'test_file.py::test_function_name') — with the pytest node id spelled out, and to record the observed harness output ('ok') at close. Applies to all three mandated additions: rebuild-before-build (Part C package), expiry re-check and gate check (Part D package).

Add to whichever package owns Part B: update backend/doorway/test_reads.py::test_the_read_count_moves_only_on_purpose from len(READS) == 29 to the new count, and settle the optional GET /runs/drift read one way or the other so the number is determinate.

Add to the Part C package two named negative tests, and make them acceptance criteria: (1) a caller naming a run that is not theirs is refused, in the database's words, with no bytes returned; (2) a run lookup that returns zero rows is a refusal, not an empty or partial document — mirroring the existing guarded invariant test_reads.py::test_a_refusal_never_arrives_as_an_empty_list. Record explicitly that cw.snapshot and its member tables carry no RLS, so the scoping rests entirely on resolving run_id through cw.run first.

Restate the Part D expiry gate against the mechanisms a test can actually induce — an inserted cw.supersession row with predecessor_disposition='retire_now', or cw.clause_version.retired set true — and name that fixture in the acceptance criteria. Record that expires_on is immutable (0002:126-155) and therefore cannot be the tested path. This correction is mandatory for planner-B, whose gate is specified against expiry columns alone.

Enumerate refusal-by-database per role rather than by exemplar. For each new endpoint state the expected outcome for all five signed-in roles (requester, legal_reviewer, legal_admin, auditor, viewer), and note that the existing parametrised sweeps in test_reads.py cover only administrator and requester so nothing is inherited.

Make 'full npm run verify green from backend/, including all three mutation harnesses (db/test/mutation-check.mjs, engine/mutation_check.py, doorway/mutation_check.py)' the last line of EVERY package's acceptance criteria, not a set-level clause. planner-A must adopt planner-B's per-package phrasing; both should carry the 'from backend/' qualifier since there is no root package.json.

Move the Part B package's prototype/v4/app/api.jsx edit either out of that package entirely (planner-B's cut) or in together with its guard in backend/db/test/shell.test.mjs, so that no package ships a file change with no test inside it.

Repair planner-B's dependency graph: remove the self-edge '{WP-005, WP-007} -> WP-007 download half' and either split WP-007 into its pre-download and download halves with an explicit edge from the Part C package, or state that WP-007 starts only after Part C lands.

Bind the service-level round trip to a non-vacuity precondition in the Part C package: assert the rebuilt snapshot has at least one member, at least one ladder rung and at least one rule consulted, so the id comparison cannot pass against an empty snapshot. Both cuts place the round trip correctly (Part C, where both endpoints first coexist, as the plan's Part F describes it) — only its vacuity is unguarded.

Reconcile planner-B's 'no migration is needed / 0024 stays free' with 0005:276-277 before packages are issued. Either the deal-ownership rule gets a database rule (planner-A's 0024) and a named two-directional test as each writing role, or the gap is recorded as a known hole with the endpoint-side check labelled as such — but the acceptance criterion 'a run cannot be recorded without a deal reference' must not be written as a database refusal it is not.

Extend shell.test.mjs's 'the viewer has no export path of any kind' assertion from viewer.jsx source to api.jsx once a download helper exists, and name that extension in the screens package that adds the helper.
blocking_issues: Three mandated mutation-harness rows are unwritable in both cuts: no pytest node ids, no find/replace strings, against a harness where MISS and SKIP are both fatal. The contract's success criterion 'break expiry re-check / gate check / rebuild-before-build must each be caught' cannot be evaluated at Gate 3 as the packages stand.

planner-B's expiry gate is specified against cw.clause_version_state's expiry columns, which are immutable (cw.clause_version_immutable(), 0002:126-155) and never pinned when already expired (selectable, 0002:256). No test can induce the condition, so the 'break the expiry re-check' mutation has no test to catch it. Must be respecified against supersession/retirement before integration.

planner-B's WP-001 acceptance requires a viewer to be refused by the database inside a package B defines as having no writes, while cw_viewer holds select on every source the loader reads (0002:352-354, 0003:669-670, 0004:237-238). The package's headline criterion is unsatisfiable as scoped.

Both cuts add READS entries in Part B without amending test_reads.py::test_the_read_count_moves_only_on_purpose (len(READS) == 29), so npm run verify is red at the close of Part B in either cut — directly contradicting the contract's closing-check requirement.

integrated.summary: Integrated Revision Plan for WS-1 (ASSEMBLY-CONNECTION-PLAN-2026-07-27.md). I adjudicated the two planner cuts and three red-team reviews against repo source, and confirmed the reviewers' central finding: BOTH planners designed Part B's run reads on cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract while asserting the database scopes them. Verified false — neither view carries a WHERE clause of its own (0005_run_store.sql:231-248), neither is security_invoker (the string appears nowhere in migrations except 0017/0019 explaining why it is the wrong tool), both are granted to cw_requester/cw_legal_reviewer/cw_legal_admin (0005:296-298), and RLS is ENABLED not FORCED, so a view runs with its owner's rights — the failure class this repo has paid for three times (0017:160-186; db/test/views-are-not-policies.test.mjs, whose catalogue only inventories cw_viewer-readable views and therefore cannot catch this one). I also confirmed planner-A right and planner-B wrong on the deal-binding rule: cw.run's write_scoped INSERT policy checks role only (0005:276-277), deliberately unlike the SELECT policy three lines above, so the SETTLED "runs are tied to deals" decision has no database rule behind it and hard constraint 2 forbids fixing it in an endpoint. Hard constraint 4 permits exactly one remedy: a package claims 0024 and records why. Selected cut: EIGHT single-owner packages WP-001..WP-008 in a strictly serial spine (transport -> A1 -> A2+0024 -> B -> C -> {D, requester screens} -> reviewer execute screen), with tests inside every package, migration 0024 owned solely by WP-003 and carrying two discovered rules (deal-ownership on insert; the two run views scoped in their own WHERE clause in the 0017/0019/0022 house style), the three named mutation-harness additions placed as writable 5-tuples with literal pytest node ids (rebuild-before-build in WP-005; expiry re-check and gate check in WP-006), and the service-level round trip in WP-005 with non-vacuity assertions. Nine further repo contradictions found by the red teams are corrected in the package text rather than in the plan file (endpoint-side agreement_executed duplicating the 0006 trigger; the docx digest wrongly fed to POST /health-checks/rebuild; missing idempotency on content-addressed snapshot/ruleset rows; cw.executed_document.kind omitted from the insert set; the READS count assertion at test_reads.py:100; expires_on immutability making planner-B's expiry gate untestable; run_drift's status filter and inner join; cw.run's immutability making the plan's "counts land on the run record" impossible after the fact; the reading-room acceptance criterion needing an EXECUTED agreement, not a recorded run). Gate 2: PASS — no genuinely new owner decision is required to issue the packages; one carried ownership question (byte transport for signature certificates after filing) is recorded as unresolved and does not block WS-1.
integrated.selected_strategy: EIGHT single-owner work packages, WP-001..WP-008, IDs stable and never renumbered, in one serial spine with a single parallel fork at the end. Order: WP-001 (transport seam) -> WP-002 (Part A1: POST /runs wired, refusing, storing nothing) -> WP-003 (Part A2: persistence + migration 0024 + audit reconciliation) -> WP-004 (Part B: three parameterless run reads) -> WP-005 (Part C: GET /runs/contract as .docx + the service-level round trip) -> {WP-006 (Part D: POST /agreements/execute), WP-007 (Part E1: requester screens)} -> WP-008 (Part E2: reviewer execute screen, after both WP-006 and WP-007). This preserves plan section 3's A->B->C->D chain exactly, honours "screens after B, execute screen after D" (screens are placed after C rather than B so the run view and the download ship together under one owner of api.jsx), and keeps Part F inside every package. Two deviations from the plan's "suggested ~six" are taken deliberately: (1) the server.py/app.py transport change is hoisted out of Part C into WP-001 so the riskiest shared file in the service has exactly one writer and is not edited at the point in the sequence with the most built on top of it; (2) Part E is split at the boundary the plan itself draws, so prototype/v4/app/api.jsx has one writer at a time. Shared-file ownership is serialised by unconditional prerequisite edges: backend/doorway/app.py is written by WP-001, WP-002, WP-005, WP-006 in that order and no two may be in flight; backend/doorway/runs.py by WP-002 then WP-003; prototype/v4/app/api.jsx by WP-007 then WP-008; backend/db/migrations/ by WP-003 alone. Test placement: F is inside every package; the three mandated mutation rows land in WP-005 (rebuild-before-build) and WP-006 (expiry re-check, gate check), each written as the literal 5-tuple backend/doorway/mutation_check.py requires including the pytest node id; the service-level round trip (record a run through POST /runs, rebuild through GET /runs/contract, snapshot id must match, as the caller) lands in WP-005, where both endpoints first coexist, named explicitly as distinct from backend/db/test/writer-sql.test.mjs and guarded against vacuity.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: The plan's suggested six-package cut, with the server.py bytes-out change left inside Part C and Part E as one package.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: Section 3 says 'Suggested work-package cut', not a constraint. Under six, backend/doorway/app.py acquires four unordered writers and Part C becomes a transport package and a document package wearing one name; Part E's own timing is already split by the plan (screens after B, execute screen after D) and its files (api.jsx, workspaces.jsx, shell.test.mjs, mutation-check.mjs) overlap. Eight buys file-level single ownership at the cost of two extra package headers.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: planner-B's position that no migration is needed and 0024 stays free (EV-233).
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: Disconfirmed at source. cw.run's write_scoped INSERT policy is `with check (cw.app_role() in ('requester','legal_reviewer','legal_admin'))` — role only, no ownership term (0005_run_store.sql:276-277) — in deliberate contrast with read_scoped directly above it, which does call cw.owns_agreement. B's claim conflates 'the schema can store agreement_id' with 'the database refuses the wrong deal'. Its WP-002 instruction 'let cw.run's RLS decide ownership' would ship POST /runs with nothing stopping a requester attaching a run to another requester's deal, permanently recorded as legitimate by the cw.audit_run trigger.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: planner-A's literal migration 0024 text: add `and (agreement_id is null or cw.owns_agreement(agreement_id))` to cw.run's write_scoped policy for all three writing roles.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: cw.owns_agreement is `a.requester = cw.app_actor()` (0003_ladders_and_concessions.sql:626-631). Legal reviewers and legal admins never appear in cw.agreement.requester, so this text refuses every run the two roles the plan explicitly permits would record — and A's own acceptance criterion ('assert both directions as each of the three writing roles') would fail. The `agreement_id is null` escape also leaves the settled deal-binding rule enforced only by an endpoint check, which A's own rationale forbids. Replaced by the two-branch shape used everywhere else in the schema (0005:271-275, 0006:276-279).

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Leaving cw.run_summary / cw.run_contract as they are and having Part B select from the RLS-bearing base tables cw.run / cw.run_decision / cw.run_finding only.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: Correct as far as the doorway goes, but it leaves two unscoped views over person-scoped data granted to three roles — the exact latent shape the repo has paid for three times — and forces reads.py to re-implement cw.run_contract's category-label and clause title/body joins, duplicating a definition the schema already owns. Retained as the stated fallback if the owner refuses migration 0024: in that case WP-004 reads base tables, the two views are added to the views-are-not-policies inventory with a recorded verdict anyway, and the deal-binding gap is carried as a named hole.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Fixing the two run views with `security_invoker = true` instead of a WHERE clause.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: The repo already rejected this in its own words for the same class of view: security_invoker evaluates the view as the caller, who then needs SELECT on every joined table (0017_reading_room.sql:175-185, restated at 0019:46). cw.run_contract joins cw.clause_version and cw.category; cw.run_summary aggregates cw.run_decision and cw.run_finding. Scoping goes in the view, stated in the same words as the policy, exactly as cw.reading_room and cw.run_drift do.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: RT2's proposal that the run selector for the document travel in a POST body (the precedent being POST /health-checks/rebuild and POST /health-checks/document, which take run_id / agreement_id + doc_seq via Write.fields, writes.py:478-492), avoiding any change to server.py's query handling.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: The plan names `GET /runs/contract` in section 2 Part C and the dependency order in section 3; pulling paper is a read, and filing it under writes.py's single-statement Write shape would misclassify a read as a write in the one pair of files that embody that distinction. Recorded as a live alternative: if the owner later prefers it, WP-001 collapses to the single bytes-out branch and the query-capture half disappears. Noted so the decision is visible rather than assumed.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Splitting Part D into an insert-set package and a gates package.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: Would permit a half-built execute endpoint that files an agreement with one of its two gates missing — a worse failure mode than a large package. Size is managed by the two named mutations and by the freeze triggers and status machine doing their existing jobs, not by cutting.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: planner-A's optional fourth Part B read, GET /runs/drift.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: A hidden unresolved decision inside a package, and it makes the mandatory edit to test_reads.py::test_the_read_count_moves_only_on_purpose unspecifiable (32 or 33). cw.run_drift is consumed by WP-006's currency gate; a drift read for the screens is a named follow-on, not part of this set.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: planner-A's placement of a prototype/v4/app/api.jsx edit inside the Part B package.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: Violates 'F lives inside every package': the only files that assert anything about api.jsx are backend/db/test/shell.test.mjs and backend/db/test/mutation-check.mjs, both owned by WP-007. api.jsx is therefore owned by WP-007 and WP-008 only; Part B ships doorway reads and their tests.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Widening backend/db/test/views-are-not-policies.test.mjs's catalogue query to every signed-in role in WP-003.

WP-003 widens to cw_requester (the role in this leak) and records the remaining widening as a named follow-on with an owner, with an in-package contingency if even the requester inventory proves larger than the package can honestly review.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: planner-B's escalation of 'signature certificates attachable after filing' to a WP-006 approval blocker.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: Settled decision 2 requires hash and signatories AT FILING and makes the certificate a later attachment; cw.signature_certificate is a separate table with its own INSERT grant (0006:532) and a nullable storage_uri, so a later insert is structurally possible. The missing piece is byte transport past a JSON-only, 1MB-capped server — a scope question for a later workstream. Carried as an unresolved ownership item, not a gate on WS-1.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Endpoint-side run_recorded and agreement_executed audit events, as the plan's Part A step 6 and Part D step 5 read.
rejected_alternatives.reason_rejected: Both are already emitted by AFTER INSERT triggers (cw.audit_run, 0005:251-263; cw.audit_executed, 0006:249-268). An endpoint copy would put two disagreeing entries per act into an append-only chain with no UPDATE or DELETE grant for any role. Endpoints write the attempt/refusal half only.

resolved_discrepancies: Part B's read source — RT1, RT2 and RT3 are right; BOTH planners are wrong. cw.run_summary (0005:250-258) and cw.run_contract (0005:239-248) carry no WHERE clause, are not security_invoker (the token appears in migrations only at 0017:175 and 0019:46, both explaining why it is the wrong tool), and are granted to cw_requester/cw_legal_reviewer/cw_legal_admin (0005:296-298). A PostgreSQL view runs with its owner's rights and RLS is ENABLED not FORCED, so cw.run's read_scoped policy is never consulted through them. planner-B's EV-216 promoted this to Observed and drew the opposite conclusion. Ruling: migration 0024 scopes both views in their own WHERE clause in the words of cw.run's read policy, per 0017/0019/0022; WP-004 then reads them safely. Verified: EV-400.

Deal binding on insert — planner-A (EV-103) is right; planner-B (EV-216, EV-233, WP-002) is wrong. 0005:276-277 checks role only. Hard constraint 2 forbids an endpoint fix; hard constraint 4 permits WP-003 to claim 0024 with a recorded reason. Verified: EV-401.

planner-A's proposed 0024 policy text — RT1 is right that it is broken. cw.owns_agreement resolves to cw.agreement.requester = cw.app_actor() (0003:626-631), so the single-condition form locks out legal_reviewer and legal_admin. Ruling: two-branch shape, `cw.app_role() in ('legal_reviewer','legal_admin') or (cw.app_role() = 'requester' and agreement_id is not null and cw.owns_agreement(agreement_id))`. Verified: EV-402.

Endpoint-side agreement_executed — RT1 and RT2 are right and planner-B (EV-205) was right first; planner-A's WP-006 reintroduced the duplication it had itself diagnosed for run_recorded. cw.audit_executed emits agreement_executed on insert into cw.executed_agreement and document_frozen on insert into cw.executed_document (0006:249-268). Ruling: endpoints write execution_attempted / execution_refused only; acceptance asserts exactly one agreement_executed per execution. Verified: EV-403.

The reading-room acceptance criterion — RT1 is right; both planners inherited an unmeetable criterion from the plan's Part B prose. cw.reading_room_clause joins cw.executed_agreement to cw.run_decision on e.run_id (0017:207-215) and cw.reading_room requires a live cw.agreement_share row (0017:186-196). A recorded run alone returns nothing. Ruling: the criterion moves to WP-006 (execution) with its real precondition — an executed agreement whose run_id is set, plus a share for a viewer — and WP-U15's 'do not fake the run' instruction travels with it. Verified: EV-404.

The rebuild spot check — RT1 is right and planner-B (EV-226) was right first; planner-A's WP-005 would have fed the .docx digest to POST /health-checks/rebuild. writes.py's own rule text states cw.record_rebuild_spot_check() compares against cw.run.result_hash (writes.py:487-491), which is Resolution.result_hash over decisions, not sha256_of(document bytes) (docx.py:167). Ruling: the document digest goes only into the document_produced audit payload; the two hashes are named side by side in WP-005 so no implementer conflates them. Verified: EV-405.

Idempotency of content-addressed rows — RT1 is right; both planners were silent. cw.snapshot and cw.ruleset are keyed by content hash (0005:64-76), so a second run against an unchanged library re-derives the same ids and a plain INSERT raises a unique violation that refusals.classify turns into a 409 'refused on merits' — a refusal that is not a refusal. writer-sql.test.mjs:126-131 already records the rule ('two runs against an unchanged library share one row … A real writer inserts them if absent') and its SHARED set is {snapshot, ruleset, ruleset_member}, omitting snapshot_member and snapshot_ladder_rung — so the writer skips the whole snapshot block when the id already exists rather than adding ON CONFLICT to three tables. Assigned to WP-003 with a named two-run test. Verified: EV-406.

cw.executed_document.kind — RT1 is right; both planners' insert sets omitted it. It is `text not null check (kind in ('agreement','amendment','exhibit','counterpart'))` with `constraint agreement_is_first check ((kind = 'agreement') = (doc_seq = 0))` (0006:60-83). Added to WP-006's required changes. Verified: EV-407.

The READS count assertion — RT3 is right; planner-A's 'all 24 existing READS' is wrong. backend/doorway/test_reads.py:100 asserts len(READS) == 29 with the message '25 ported plus 4 added on purpose'. Three new reads means that number moves to 32 in the same package, or npm run verify closes Part B red. Verified: EV-408.

Mutation-row writability — RT3 is right. backend/doorway/mutation_check.py rows are 5-tuples whose fifth element is a literal pytest node id, and MISS and SKIP are both fatal (mutation_check.py:55-77). Neither planner supplied node ids or find/replace strings, and RT1 is additionally right that planner-A's WP-001 row for a query parameter nothing consumes cannot be written at all. Ruling: every mutation row is stated verbatim in its package; WP-001 carries only the bytes-path row (which has a real unit test in test_server.py); the query-selector row moves to WP-005, its first consumer. planner-A's phrasing 'go from ok to MISS when removed' is also backwards — deleting guarded code makes the find string absent and yields SKIP. Verified: EV-409.

The expiry gate's testable mechanism — RT3 is right and planner-B's specification is unworkable. cw.clause_version.expires_on is immutable: cw.clause_version_immutable() raises restrict_violation on any change to it and the clause_version_no_edit trigger fires before update (0002:126-158), and an already-expired version is not selectable so is never pinned. A date-based lapse between run and signature cannot be induced in a test. Ruling: WP-006's gate is specified against currency as a whole — supersession (cw.supersession with predecessor_disposition = 'retire_now') and retirement — with the fixture named in the acceptance criteria, and expiry checked but recorded as the branch no test can induce. Verified: EV-410.

cw.run_drift as the gate's source — planner-A was right that it is the one view already joining on the pinned (clause_id, version), and RT1/RT2 are right that it is not a complete gate: it inner-joins cw.agreement (a run with a null agreement_id is invisible), filters `a.status <> 'executed'`, emits only rows already flagged as superseded or non-active, and is documented REPORTING ONLY (0022:173-208). RT2 is additionally right that the gate must be evaluated BEFORE the cw.executed_agreement insert, whose trigger moves the agreement to executed (0006:206-211) and empties the view for that run. All three constraints are written into WP-006. Verified: EV-411.

Provenance counts — RT1 is right and neither planner surfaced it. The plan's Part C item 2 says 'the counts land on the run record', but cw.run holds select+insert grants only (0005:288-290) and carries run_immutable no_edit/no_delete/no_truncate triggers (0005:188-214), while engine/docx.py:403-414 computes the counts from document bytes. Nothing can land on the run record after insert. Ruling (settleable from source, recorded in WP-003 with the alternative): POST /runs builds the document in memory solely to compute provenance_counts and discards it, so the record is complete and honest at insert time; the alternative — permanent zeros, which engine/run.py:214-219 blesses only for 'a run that emitted no document' — is recorded, and if the owner prefers it the plan's Part C sentence is void. Verified: EV-412.

cw.audit_event INSERT grants — RT1 is right that planner-A's EV-107 is stale: 0013_administrator.sql:257 also grants insert, select to cw_administrator, with an insert policy at 0013:275. planner-A's derived conclusion (an auditor cannot download, because the chain refuses their insert) survives; the enumeration does not. Consequence added to WP-002: an administrator passes the audit gate but holds no cw.run INSERT, so POST /runs refuses them only once WP-003 lands — a stated, temporary uniformity gap with its closing package named. Verified: EV-413.

planner-B's WP-001 viewer criterion — RT2 and RT3 are right that it is unsatisfiable as scoped. cw_viewer holds SELECT on cw.clause_version_state and cw.selectable_clause (0002:352-354), the ladder tables (0003:669-670) and cw.active_conflict_rule (0004:237-238), so a write-free POST /runs refuses nobody. Ruling: planner-A's shape is adopted — WP-002 writes the attempt row first through cw.audit (language sql, not SECURITY DEFINER), so the database refuses at the boundary in its own words, preserving the manifests.py uniformity argument (manifests.py:203-222). Verified: EV-414.

Dependency-graph defects — RT1/RT2/RT3 are right on both. planner-B's '{WP-005, WP-007} -> WP-007 download half' makes a package its own prerequisite; planner-A's graph ('WP-004 -> {WP-005 -> WP-006, WP-007}') contradicts its own WP-007 text and hedges WP-002's prerequisite as 'none strictly'. Ruling: every edge in the selected cut is unconditional, WP-007 sits after WP-005 so the run view and the download ship together, and file ownership is whole-file, never 'the write half of runs.py'.

Screen line anchors — RT1 is right. The requester's NotBuiltYet is at prototype/v4/app/requester.jsx:343 ('Intake, the manifest, the forge and the validate findings are not built.'); the 'the forge that produces runs is not built yet' caption is at :338. planner-A cited 335, planner-B cited 315-336. Corrected in WP-007. Verified: EV-415.

Unscoped snapshot tables — RT1, RT2 and RT3 are right that both planners were silent. 0005:265-268 enables RLS on cw.run, cw.run_decision and cw.run_finding only; cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member, cw.snapshot_ladder_rung, cw.ruleset and cw.ruleset_member carry none while being granted to four roles (0005:288-295). Both planners correctly route Part C's rebuild to those base tables (cw.run_snapshot is auditor-only) without noting that all the scoping therefore rests on resolving run_id through cw.run first. Written into WP-005 as a recorded decision with two named negative tests. Verified: EV-417.

Both planners' shared corrections to the plan text, verified and carried into the package headers rather than into the plan file: the engine reads cw.active_conflict_rule, not cw.conflict_rule (loader.py:50-54); the loader's public snapshot entry is build_snapshot (loader.py:133); npm run verify runs THREE mutation harnesses, not two (backend/package.json), and must be invoked from backend/; cw.run.engine_version is NOT NULL with no default and is absent from the plan's Part A step 5 list (0005:97-108); manifests.manifest_from accepts any 'source' string while cw.run.manifest_source is constrained to ('llm','fallback','manual') (manifests.py:100; 0005:88). Ruling on the last: WP-002 validates at the boundary in runs.py and returns a 400 naming the field, rather than tightening manifest_from — so POST /manifests/check's live behaviour is unchanged, which settles planner-B's open question about the two endpoints disagreeing.
unresolved_issues: Byte transport for a signature certificate attached AFTER filing has no owner. Settled decision 2 (memory.md, 2026-07-27) makes the certificate a later attachment and WP-006 files hash and signatories at filing exactly as that decision requires, so this does not block WS-1. But cw.signature_certificate.certificate is bytea NOT NULL with octet_length > 0 (0006:312-324), the table carries frozen/no_delete triggers, backend/doorway/server.py reads JSON only under MAX_BODY = 1_000_000 (server.py:56), and GAP-CLOSURE-PLAN scopes WS-8 as the byte store and the e-signature provider rather than this act. Whether the act belongs to WS-8, to a new package, or to a later WS-1 addendum is a scope/ownership question only the owner can answer. Tagged Unresolved (EV-418); carried, not resolved by this plan. Note the one degree of freedom already in the schema: cw.signature_certificate.storage_uri is nullable (0006:322), unlike cw.executed_document.storage_uri.

Whether an auditor should be able to download a pre-execution contract. The house pattern (audit recorded through the caller's own connection, manifests.py:203-222) plus the audit INSERT grants (cw_requester, cw_legal_reviewer, cw_legal_admin, cw_administrator — 0001:339-346, 0013:257) means an auditor holding SELECT on every run is refused the download by the chain rather than by the run. This plan SETTLES it in favour of the house pattern (the alternative — auditing outside the caller's transaction — reintroduces the privileged path db.py exists to make impossible) and requires WP-005 to record it as a decision with a named test. It is listed here only so the owner sees a consequence they may wish to reverse later; it is not a blocker and no package waits on it.

The size of the views-are-not-policies widening is not knowable without running the harness. WP-003 widens the catalogue query from cw_viewer to cw_viewer + cw_requester so the two run views can be inventoried at all (the existing ghost check at views-are-not-policies.test.mjs:142-150 fails if a REVIEWED entry is not viewer-readable, so entries cannot simply be added). The migrations define roughly 55 views against a 21-entry inventory. If the requester-readable inventory proves larger than WP-003 can honestly review, the package narrows to the two run views plus an explicit named follow-on with an owner — an in-package contingency, recorded, not a hidden decision.
final_actions: Issue the eight packages WP-001..WP-008 with the IDs fixed; no renumbering, no reordering, every prerequisite edge unconditional.

Before WP-003 begins, put migration 0024's two rules in front of the owner as a claim (not a question): cw.run's INSERT policy checks role only and the SETTLED deal-binding decision has no rule behind it; cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract bypass cw.run's read policy by owner-rights. Hard constraint 4 already authorises a package to claim 0024 with a recorded reason; the migration header states both discovered facts and cites hard constraint 2 as why an endpoint cannot fix either.

Do not edit ASSEMBLY-CONNECTION-PLAN-2026-07-27.md. Carry its nine verified contradictions in the package headers instead, each with its source line: cw.active_conflict_rule not cw.conflict_rule; build_snapshot as the loader entry; run_recorded and agreement_executed emitted by triggers; three mutation harnesses not two; Part C's server change is two files not one; Part C item 2's 'the counts land on the run record' is impossible against an immutable cw.run; Part B's 'GET /reading-room/clauses returns rows with no further code' needs an executed agreement plus a share; engine_version missing from Part A step 5; storage_uri is NOT NULL with WS-8 out of scope.

Write every mutation row verbatim in its owning package as the 5-tuple backend/doorway/mutation_check.py expects — (name, file, find, replace, 'test_file.py::test_function_name') — with the pytest node id spelled out, and record the harness's observed verdict ('ok') at package close.

Make 'npm run verify green from backend/, including all three mutation harnesses (db/test/mutation-check.mjs, engine/mutation_check.py, doorway/mutation_check.py)' the last acceptance line of EVERY package, not a set-level clause.
Require every package to carry an explicit rollback note; neither planner supplied them and the objective contract asks for one per package.

Seed synthetic conflict rules, clauses and ladders as development data in WP-002 under the placeholder-content rule, so validate() is exercised against a non-empty catalogue and 'zero rules reads as zero' is tested as the other case rather than the only one.

Record, in WP-005 and WP-006 respectively, the two decisions the packages must not leave to an implementer: which hash goes where (document digest to the audit payload; recomputed result_hash to POST /health-checks/rebuild), and whether the execution gates are endpoint logic or a trigger (endpoint, with the comparison written down, because hard constraint 2 governs WHO may act rather than WHETHER an act is currently valid).
Spawn a named follow-on, with an owner, for the residual views-are-not-policies widening beyond cw_viewer + cw_requester, and a second for the byte transport of post-filing signature certificates.
work_package_strategy: WP-001 · Transport seam (Part C's server change, hoisted). OWNER: doorway. PREREQUISITES: none. TARGET FILES: backend/doorway/app.py, backend/doorway/server.py, backend/doorway/test_server.py, backend/doorway/mutation_check.py. CHANGES: (a) give app.Response a bytes-carrying sibling (status, bytes, content type, filename, content-length) so app.py can express a download without server.py learning about runs — Response.body is typed dict today (app.py:48-51) and server._respond unconditionally json.dumps with application/json (server.py:178-185); (b) stop discarding the query string in do_GET/_endpoint (server.py:78-88) and pass ONE whitelisted selector through to App.handle — captured and consumed by nothing in this package; (c) every existing JSON endpoint's response byte-identical. No engine call, no SQL, no screen, no new route. TESTS INSIDE: a unit test in test_server.py that a bytes response leaves with the .docx content type, the filename and a correct content-length; a test that a query string reaches App.handle; the existing doorway suite unchanged. ONE mutation row only — the bytes branch serialised as JSON, guarded by the named unit test. NO mutation row for the query capture (nothing consumes it; MISS and SKIP are both fatal) — that row is WP-005's. DECISION RECORDED: why the selector travels in the URL rather than in a POST body (the plan names GET /runs/contract; a document read is a read and writes.py's single-statement Write shape would misfile it), with RT2's body-carried alternative named so a later owner can collapse this package. ROLLBACK: revert two source files; nothing depends on it until WP-005.

WP-002 · Part A1: POST /runs wired, refusing, storing nothing. OWNER: doorway. PREREQUISITES: WP-001 (unconditional — app.py single-writer ordering). TARGET FILES: backend/doorway/runs.py (NEW), backend/doorway/app.py (one dispatch line), backend/doorway/test_runs.py (NEW), backend/db/test/loader-sql.test.mjs (extend). CHANGES: a module in the manifests.py shape, not a writes.py entry (Write holds one statement, writes.py:119-147); manifests.manifest_from for the body and check_manifest re-run against categories_for; manifest_source validated at the boundary against ('llm','fallback','manual') with a 400 naming the field, so a bad source is never a late 409 — validated in runs.py, NOT by tightening manifest_from, leaving POST /manifests/check's live behaviour unchanged; CLAUSE_SQL / RULE_SQL / LADDER_SQL run over the caller's own Request via loader.build_snapshot and build_ruleset; resolve() then validate(); the answer states how many rules were consulted so zero reads as zero. The attempt row (run_attempted / run_refused) is written through cw.audit FIRST, so a viewer or auditor is refused by the database before any engine answer is reported — the manifests.py uniformity rule. NO persistence, no run id, never run_recorded. Synthetic conflict rules, clauses and ladders seeded as development data. TESTS INSIDE: viewer refused by the database in its own words; a dropped category refused with check_manifest's own sentence; an empty library refuses loudly with SnapshotIncomplete's words and never returns a partial run; a rungless ladder refuses with the engine's error; nothing lands in cw.run; loader-sql.test.mjs runs all three loader queries (it already extracts RULE_SQL) as each of the five roles against the migrated schema. RECORDED GAP: cw_administrator holds audit INSERT (0013:257) but no cw.run INSERT, so an administrator receives an answer until WP-003 lands — stated, with WP-003 named as the closing package. ROLLBACK: delete runs.py and its dispatch line; the audit vocabulary introduced here is permanent (cw.audit_event has no UPDATE or DELETE grant), so the event names are fixed in this package on purpose.

WP-003 · Part A2: persistence, the two database rules, audit reconciliation. OWNER: doorway + db (one owner, two surfaces). PREREQUISITES: WP-002. TARGET FILES: backend/doorway/runs.py, backend/db/migrations/0024_runs_belong_to_the_callers_deal_and_the_run_views_scope_themselves.sql (NEW — claims 0024, the only migration in the whole set), backend/db/test/run-store.test.mjs, backend/db/test/writer-sql.test.mjs, backend/db/test/views-are-not-policies.test.mjs, backend/doorway/test_runs.py, backend/doorway/mutation_check.py. MIGRATION 0024, two discovered rules in one file with both reasons in the header: (a) replace cw.run's write_scoped INSERT policy — no CREATE OR REPLACE POLICY exists, so ALTER POLICY or an explicit DROP+CREATE naming write_scoped — with the two-branch house shape `cw.app_role() in ('legal_reviewer','legal_admin') or (cw.app_role() = 'requester' and agreement_id is not null and cw.owns_agreement(agreement_id))`, matching 0005:271-275 and 0006:276-279; (b) recreate cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract with the scoping IN THE VIEW, in the same words as cw.run's read_scoped policy (cw.run_contract must join cw.run to do it), NOT security_invoker, for the reason 0017:175-185 records; (c) widen views-are-not-policies.test.mjs's catalogue query from cw_viewer to cw_viewer + cw_requester and add both run views to REVIEWED with the verdict 'scoped'. DOORWAY CHANGES: snapshot_rows / ruleset_rows / run_rows inserted through the caller's connection in one transaction (db.Request has no executemany — the loop is hand-written and a partial failure rolls the whole run back); content-addressed rows inserted only when absent — the whole snapshot block skipped when snapshot_id already exists and the ruleset block when ruleset_id does, per writer-sql.test.mjs:126-131, noting snapshot_member and snapshot_ladder_rung are NOT in that file's SHARED set; run id generated server-side as uuid4 hex (DECISION RECORDED: not a content hash, because two runs of an unchanged manifest against an unchanged library would collide, and cw.run.run_id has no default); agreement_id required by the endpoint's shape and enforced by 0024's policy; engine_version from engine.model.ENGINE_VERSION; provenance counts DECISION RECORDED — the document is built in memory at record time solely to compute provenance_counts and discarded, because cw.run is immutable with no UPDATE grant so the plan's 'counts land on the run record' can never happen later; the zero alternative is recorded with engine/run.py:214-219's blessing quoted. Audit: endpoint writes run_attempted / run_refused only. TESTS INSIDE: a requester recording a run against another requester's deal is refused BY THE DATABASE, both in test_runs.py and in run-store.test.mjs, asserted in both directions for all three writing roles including legal_reviewer and legal_admin recording on deals they do not own; exactly one run_recorded per run (the trigger's); cw.run.engine_version equals ENGINE_VERSION; two runs against an unchanged library produce one snapshot row and two run rows; a bad manifest source is a 400 not a 409; cw.run's other policies (read_scoped, 0013's administrator_reads) survive 0024 unchanged; the run views return only the caller's rows per role. ROLLBACK: the migration is additive-by-replacement — the rollback note states the prior policy text and the prior view definitions verbatim so 0024 can be reversed by a 0025 that restores them; no data is destroyed.

WP-004 · Part B: read runs back. OWNER: doorway. PREREQUISITES: WP-003 (needs both 0024 rules and real runs). TARGET FILES: backend/doorway/reads.py, backend/doorway/test_reads.py. CHANGES: exactly three new READS entries — GET /runs from the now-scoped cw.run_summary, GET /runs/decisions from the now-scoped cw.run_contract, GET /runs/findings from the RLS-bearing base table cw.run_finding — each naming the policy or view clause it defers to, as every existing entry does. All parameterless: the reading-room control at reads.py:276-287 is preserved rather than broken, and the package RECORDS that choice and its rationale. No fourth 'drift' read (kept out so the READS count is determinate; a drift read is a named follow-on).
