risk_register: Migration 0024 replaces an existing policy on cw.run, a table that also carries immutability triggers and 0013's administrator_reads. PostgreSQL has no CREATE OR REPLACE POLICY, so 0024 must ALTER POLICY write_scoped ON cw.run or DROP+CREATE it by name; a rename mismatch or a wrong drop leaves cw.run momentarily without a write policy — which fails closed, but surfaces as a confusing refusal. MITIGATION: run-store.test.mjs asserts both directions for all three writing roles AND asserts that cw.run's other policies survive 0024 unchanged; the rollback note carries the prior policy text verbatim.

0024 also recreates two views. Recreating cw.run_contract requires adding a join to cw.run, which changes its row shape's provenance if any existing consumer selects from it. MITIGATION: grep for existing consumers before the rewrite (none expected — the reads are new) and assert the auditor still sees every run through both views.

WP-001 changes the one file every endpoint passes through. A careless branch could serialise a dict as bytes or leak a stack trace through the new path. MITIGATION: no endpoint consumes the new capability in WP-001; the query selector is captured and ignored; every existing JSON response is asserted byte-identical; one mutation row guards the bytes branch.

backend/doorway/app.py is written by four packages (WP-001, WP-002, WP-005, WP-006). The no-concurrent-mutation guarantee rests entirely on those edges being hard. MITIGATION: every edge is unconditional; the dispatch lines are additive and adjacent; no two of the four may be in flight simultaneously.

prototype/v4/app/api.jsx is written by WP-007 then WP-008 and is the file the no-broad-fetch rule lives in. MITIGATION: WP-007 argues the run-id and download rationale once; WP-008 adds one execute call and extends the viewer-export assertion rather than re-opening the rule.

POST /runs is a long multi-insert transaction through a role-bound connection and db.Request exposes no executemany. A partial failure must roll the whole run back — a half-written run is worse than no run. MITIGATION: one transaction, hand-written loop, a named test that a mid-insert failure leaves cw.run empty.

Content-addressed snapshot and ruleset ids repeat across runs against an unchanged library, so a naive INSERT raises a unique violation that refusals.classify turns into a 409 'refused on merits' — a refusal that is not a refusal. MITIGATION: WP-003 skips the whole snapshot block and the ruleset block when the id already exists, with a named two-run test asserting one snapshot row and two run rows.

cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member, cw.snapshot_ladder_rung, cw.ruleset and cw.ruleset_member carry NO row-level security while being granted to four roles. The document endpoint is the first place a caller-supplied identifier reaches an unscoped table, and the audit chain will record any resulting download as legitimate. MITIGATION: WP-005 resolves the selector through cw.run FIRST and treats zero rows as a refusal, with a named negative test for another caller's run.

Recording document_produced through the caller's connection denies the download to auditors and viewers. If judged wrong later, the alternative (auditing outside the caller's transaction) reintroduces the privileged path db.py exists to make impossible. MITIGATION: recorded as a decision in WP-005 with its test, not discovered during an acceptance sweep.

A gate built on it alone passes silently for a run with a null agreement_id and for a clause that is active but imminently expiring. MITIGATION: WP-006 evaluates the gate before the executed_agreement insert, adds the direct cw.clause_version_state check for null-agreement runs, and names both branches in its acceptance.

evidence_items.claim: cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract carry no scoping expression of their own, are not security_invoker, and are granted to cw_requester, cw_legal_reviewer and cw_legal_admin; since a PostgreSQL view runs with its owner's rights and RLS here is ENABLED rather than FORCED, cw.run's read_scoped policy is never consulted through them. The existing guard cannot catch it because its catalogue query filters on has_table_privilege('cw_viewer', ...).
evidence_items.source: backend/db/migrations/0005_run_store.sql:231-248 (run_contract), :250-258 (run_summary), :296-298 (grants); no occurrence of security_invoker in any migration except 0017_reading_room.sql:175 and 0019_override_views_scoped.sql:46, both explaining why it is the wrong tool; the rule stated at 0017:160-186; backend/db/test/views-are-not-policies.test.mjs:120-150

evidence_items.source: backend/db/migrations/0003_ladders_and_concessions.sql:626-631; the two-branch house shape appears at 0005:271-275 and 0003:643-645

evidence_items.claim: cw.audit_executed() emits agreement_executed on AFTER INSERT on cw.executed_agreement and document_frozen on AFTER INSERT on cw.executed_document, so an endpoint-side agreement_executed would double-record into a chain with no UPDATE or DELETE grant.
evidence_items.source: backend/db/migrations/0006_executed_agreements.sql:249-268; cf. cw.audit_run at 0005:251-263 (planner-A EV-105, planner-B EV-205)

evidence_items.claim: cw.reading_room_clause joins cw.executed_agreement to cw.run_decision on e.run_id, and cw.reading_room requires an unrevoked cw.agreement_share row, so GET /reading-room/clauses cannot return rows from a recorded run alone — it needs an EXECUTED agreement whose run_id is set, plus a share for a viewer.
evidence_items.source: backend/db/migrations/0017_reading_room.sql:186-215; contradicts ASSEMBLY-CONNECTION-PLAN-2026-07-27.md Part B ('After Part A records a genuine run … it returns rows with no further code')

evidence_items.claim: POST /health-checks/rebuild's own rule text states cw.record_rebuild_spot_check() compares against cw.run.result_hash, which is Resolution.result_hash over decisions — not sha256_of(document bytes).

cw.snapshot and cw.ruleset are content-addressed primary keys, and the repo's own writer test records the consequence: two runs against an unchanged library share one row and 'a real writer inserts them if absent'. Its SHARED set is {snapshot, ruleset, ruleset_member} and omits snapshot_member and snapshot_ladder_rung.

cw.executed_document.kind is text NOT NULL constrained to ('agreement','amendment','exhibit','counterpart') with `constraint agreement_is_first check ((kind = 'agreement') = (doc_seq = 0))`; neither planner's insert set named it.
backend/doorway/test_reads.py asserts len(READS) == 29 ('25 ported plus 4 added on purpose'), so any package adding reads must move that number in the same package or npm run verify closes red.

backend/doorway/mutation_check.py's MUTATIONS rows are 5-tuples whose fifth element is a literal pytest node id (e.g. 'test_writes.py::test_a_write_lands_with_the_signed_in_person_s_name_on_it'), and both MISS and SKIP are fatal — so a mutation guarding a capability no test consumes cannot be authored.

cw.clause_version.expires_on is immutable — cw.clause_version_immutable() raises restrict_violation on any change to expires_on and clause_version_no_edit fires before update — so a date-based lapse between run and signature cannot be induced in a test; the inducible currency changes are supersession and retirement.

cw.run_drift joins cw.run to cw.run_decision to cw.clause_version_state on the pinned (clause_id, version) and scopes itself in its own WHERE clause, but inner-joins cw.agreement, filters `a.status <> 'executed'`, emits only rows where a supersession exists or the current state is not active, and is documented REPORTING ONLY. cw.executed_agreement's insert trigger moves the agreement to executed.

packages.title: Transport seam — the doorway learns to send bytes, and to see one query selector
packages.objective: Give backend/doorway/app.py a bytes-carrying response type and teach backend/doorway/server.py to send it, and stop server.py discarding the query string — both hoisted out of Part C so the two files every endpoint passes through have exactly one writer, before anything is built on top of them. required_changes: 0024 header: state all three discovered facts in full, with their sources and the constraint that authorises the file. (a) cw.run's write_scoped INSERT policy checks role only — `with check (cw.app_role() in ('requester','legal_reviewer','legal_admin'))` (0005_run_store.sql:276-277) — deliberately unlike the read_scoped policy three lines above it, which does call cw.owns_agreement. The settled owner decision of 2026-07-27 ('every assembly run belongs to a deal') says the database's existing row rules decide whose deal a requester may run against; they do not, and hard constraint 2 forbids fixing it in an endpoint. (b) cw.run_decision's and cw.run_finding's INSERT policies check role only in the same way (0005:281-286), so a requester could append decisions and findings to another requester's run, permanently, into immutable tables. (c) cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract carry no scoping expression of their own, are not security_invoker, and are granted to cw_requester, cw_legal_reviewer and cw_legal_admin (0005:231-248, 296-298) — a view runs with its owner's rights and row-level security here is ENABLED not FORCED, so cw.run's read policy is never consulted through them. That is the failure this repo has paid for three times (0017_reading_room.sql:160-186).

0024 rule (a): `drop policy write_scoped on cw.run;` then `create policy write_scoped on cw.run for insert with check (cw.app_role() in ('legal_reviewer','legal_admin') or (cw.app_role() = 'requester' and agreement_id is not null and cw.owns_agreement(agreement_id)));`. DROP+CREATE by name rather than ALTER POLICY, so the rollback is symmetrical and the prior text is quotable verbatim. The two-branch shape is the house shape (0005:271-275, 0006_executed_agreements.sql:276-279); the single-condition form is refused because cw.owns_agreement resolves to `a.requester = cw.app_actor()` (0003_ladders_and_concessions.sql:626-631) and would lock out legal_reviewer and legal_admin, who never appear in cw.agreement.requester.

0024 rule (b), MANDATORY in this package and not conditional: `drop policy write_scoped on cw.run_decision;` / `create policy write_scoped on cw.run_decision for insert with check (exists (select 1 from cw.run r where r.run_id = run_decision.run_id));` and the identical pair for cw.run_finding. The subquery is evaluated under row-level security, so it means 'a run this caller can see', which is exactly the read_scoped policy above it. It ships with (a) because without it rule (a) is bypassable one table over: a requester refused a run row on somebody else's deal can still append decisions and findings to that run, into tables with no UPDATE or DELETE grant. Fixing that in an endpoint is forbidden by hard constraint 2, and 0024 is the only file in the set that may carry a database rule.

0024 rule (c): `create or replace view cw.run_summary as ... from cw.run r where cw.app_role() in ('legal_reviewer','legal_admin','auditor','administrator') or (cw.app_role() = 'requester' and (r.created_by = cw.app_actor() or (r.agreement_id is not null and cw.owns_agreement(r.agreement_id))));` — the same words as cw.run's read_scoped policy (0005:271-275), stated in the view, in the style of cw.run_drift (0022:196-200), cw.override_passes (0019:95-105) and cw.reading_room. The existing select list (0005:240-248) is preserved exactly, so CREATE OR REPLACE is sufficient.

0024 rule (c) continued: `create or replace view cw.run_contract as ...` with `join cw.run r on r.run_id = d.run_id` added and the same WHERE clause, preserving the existing column list and its `order by d.run_id, d.seq` (0005:231-238). The join is required because the view selects from cw.run_decision and has no run row to scope against otherwise. NOT security_invoker — 0017:175-185 and 0019:46 already record, in this repo's own words, why that is the wrong tool for a view joining tables the caller may not hold SELECT on.

runs.py: after validate(), inside the SAME `with db.as_person(...)` block WP-002 opened, insert in this order — cw.snapshot, cw.snapshot_member, cw.snapshot_ladder_rung, cw.ruleset, cw.ruleset_member, cw.run, cw.run_decision, cw.run_finding — using engine.run.snapshot_rows(snapshot, categories), engine.run.ruleset_rows(ruleset) and engine.run.run_rows(...). db.Request exposes no executemany (db.py:92-146), so the loop is hand-written; the whole block is one transaction and a partial failure rolls the entire run back.

The bytes are discarded and never stored. DOCUMENT-DATE NOTE, recorded beside the call and cross-referenced from WP-005: build_docx stamps `Dated: <today>` from `today or date.today()` (docx.py:113-123), so this in-memory build is date-dependent — but ai_originated_characters matches whole paragraphs against AI-drafted clause BODIES (docx.py:390-400), and the date paragraph is never one, so the stamp cannot move the number. This build therefore takes the default date deliberately and the bytes are never compared with anything. WP-005, which returns bytes to a caller, does NOT take the default — it passes today from cw.run.created_at.

implementation_notes: Migration 0024 carries THREE rules and all three are mandatory. Rule (b) was not in the plan's authorised list and is settled here rather than left conditional: without it rule (a) is bypassable one table over, hard constraint 2 forbids the endpoint fix, and 0024 is the only file in the set that may carry a database rule. It is two policy pairs and two tests. The header records it as a discovered fact alongside (a) and (c), with its source line (0005:281-286), so the owner reads the reason in the migration rather than in a package note.

Provenance-count decision, recorded with BOTH alternatives so no implementer has to guess. engine.docx.provenance_counts(data, resolution, structural) (docx.py:403-415) requires an explicit `structural` list of the document's own literal strings, and the only thing that builds one is test code. Having the doorway build it would put a second copy of build_docx's literals in another file — the drift this repo has paid for repeatedly. So ai_origin_chars is computed honestly, and authored_chars is recorded as 0 by construction, justified by the engine's own standing assertion that build_docx emits zero authored characters rather than by not having looked. Alternative A: duplicate the structural vocabulary in the doorway and compute both figures. Alternative B: record both as zero, which engine/run.py:214-219 blesses only for 'a run that emitted no document' and which would make the plan's Part C sentence void. Either costs one function in runs.py and no migration.

Decision recorded: the views-are-not-policies catalogue query is NOT widened. Measured against the migrated schema: cw_viewer can read 21 views, cw_requester 29, and the eight requester-only views are cw.concession_in_force, cw.concession_state, cw.position_current, cw.position_revival, cw.renewal_drift, cw.run_contract, cw.run_drift and cw.run_summary. cw.run_drift already scopes itself, and FIVE of the remaining six read person-scoped tables without scoping. Widening would fail the harness on five views owned by WS-6 and the concession family, inside a WS-1 package. The plan's own contingency is triggered and the named targeted test above is the narrow form.

Note for whoever picks up that follow-on: the harness's reverse check would NOT have flagged cw.run_contract even after widening, because its risky-table set is textual and cw.run_decision's read policy scopes transitively through cw.run rather than naming app_actor or owns_agreement itself. The check has a blind spot for one-hop scoping.
0024 must not touch cw.run's read_scoped policy or 0013's administrator_reads. Drop by name, create by name, and assert the survivors.

executions.py DEAL BINDING, evaluated before every other gate: refuse with 409 when `run["agreement_id"] is None` — 'this run is not tied to a deal, so it cannot be filed against one' — and refuse with 409 naming BOTH when `run["agreement_id"] != agreement_id` — 'run {run_id} was recorded against {run_agreement}, not {agreement_id}'. cw.executed_agreement.run_id is a plain nullable FK to cw.run with no constraint tying it to agreement_id (0006:20-25), and after 0024 a legal_reviewer or legal_admin may record a run against any deal or none, so without this check Legal could file AG-2 citing a run recorded against AG-1, permanently, with cw.audit_executed recording it as legitimate. Refusing a null-agreement run is the settled decision of 2026-07-27 ('every assembly run belongs to a deal') applied at the only act that consumes one; the rule is stated in the module docstring with that decision named.

executions.py CURRENCY GATE (the plan's 'expiry re-check'), evaluated BEFORE any insert into cw.executed_agreement. THE PRIMARY QUERY IS THE DIRECT ONE, because it is complete: `select d.clause_id, d.version, s.state from cw.run_decision d join cw.clause_version_state s on s.clause_id = d.clause_id and s.version = d.version where d.run_id = %s and d.clause_id is not null and s.state <> 'active'` — cw.clause_version_state derives superseded, retired, expired and active in one place (0002:221-258). cw.run_drift is then consulted as CORROBORATION ONLY, for the successor_version detail it already computes (0022:173-208), and never as the gate: it inner-joins cw.agreement, filters `a.status <> 'executed'`, emits only rows already flagged, and declares itself REPORTING ONLY. Any row from the primary query refuses with 409 naming the clause and its state: 'this run carries {clause_id}@v{version}, which is {state} — it cannot be executed as it stands'.

executions.py: the ordering constraint is load-bearing and must be commented — the cw.executed_agreement insert fires cw.agreement_execute(), which moves the agreement to 'executed' (0006:194-212), and cw.run_drift then returns nothing for that run. A gate evaluated after the insert passes vacuously, forever.

executions.py VALIDATION GATE — READ THIS PARAGRAPH BEFORE WRITING THE CODE. cw.run.gate_open and cw.run.overridden are written once at insert and can NEVER change: cw.run carries run_immutable no_edit/no_delete/no_truncate triggers (0005:188-214) and holds select+insert grants only (0005:288-291), and nothing in migrations 0001-0023 updates cw.run. So `overridden` is NOT the answer to 'was this gate opened' — the human override apparatus lives entirely in 0015: an approval is one row per individually approved finding, and cw.override_passes is the load-bearing view of what an approval actually lets past (0015:364-374, rescoped at 0019:95-105). The gate is therefore: (1) `if run["gate_open"]:` proceed — gate_open is the trigger for consulting the override tables, never the answer; (2) otherwise read the blocking findings, `select seq, rule_id, rule_version, title from cw.run_finding where run_id = %s and severity = 'High' order by seq`; (3) read the passes, `select finding_ref from cw.override_passes where run_id = %s` — the view is already scoped to the caller (0019) and already requires decision = 'approved' plus a socialisation row, and cw.decide_override_finding refuses a decision before the review window closes (0015:314-318), so window closure is enforced upstream and this endpoint does not re-implement it; (4) refuse with 409 when ANY blocking finding has no matching pass, naming the finding: 'this run is blocked by {rule_id}@v{rule_version} ({title}) and no approved override covers it'.

executions.py THE FINDING REFERENCE, stated because it is otherwise an unresolved decision hidden inside a package: cw.override_finding.finding_ref is free text (0015:78-99) and cw.run_finding has no ref column of its own, so the mapping must be fixed somewhere and this is the place. Define one module-level function — `def finding_ref(row) -> str: return f"{row['rule_id']}@v{row['rule_version']}"` — matching engine ConflictRule.ref (validation.py:49-51) and cw.conflict_rule's own audit vocabulary (0004:190). A pass matches when `finding_ref = %(ref)s or finding_ref like %(suffix)s` with suffix = '%:' || ref, which admits the optional `category:` prefix 0015's watcher matching relies on (0015:220-228); rule_id is constrained to `^[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$` (0004:40) and contains no colon, so the match is deterministic. Matching is fail-closed: a reference that does not match refuses. WP-007 makes the requester's override form emit this exact reference; the consequence for category-watcher matching is recorded in open issues with a named follow-on.

executions.py inserts, in this order, all inside the caller's single transaction after all three gates have passed: (1) `insert into cw.executed_agreement (agreement_id, run_id, executed_on, effective_on, term_end, agreement_kind, parent_agreement_id, signature_evidence) values (...)`; (2) `insert into cw.executed_document (agreement_id, doc_seq, kind, filename, byte_size, sha256, storage_uri, signed_on) values (%(agreement_id)s, 0, 'agreement', ...)` — kind is NOT NULL against a closed set and the constraint agreement_is_first requires (kind='agreement') = (doc_seq=0) (0006:60-83), and both planners' insert sets omitted it; (3) one `insert into cw.executed_signatory (agreement_id, ordinal, name, party, method, signed_on, title)` per signatory.

executions.py: the endpoint writes execution_attempted / execution_refused and NOTHING ELSE into the chain. cw.audit_executed() emits agreement_executed on insert into cw.executed_agreement and document_frozen on insert into cw.executed_document (0006:249-268); an endpoint copy would put two disagreeing entries per act into a chain with no UPDATE or DELETE grant.

implementation_notes: Recorded, because it changes what the test can honestly claim: cw.clause_version.expires_on is IMMUTABLE — cw.clause_version_immutable() raises restrict_violation on any change to it and clause_version_no_edit fires before update (0002:126-158) — and an already-expired version is not selectable, so it is never pinned into a run in the first place. A date-based lapse between run and signature therefore cannot be induced in a test. The gate is specified against CURRENCY AS A WHOLE via cw.clause_version_state, whose `state` covers superseded, retired AND expired (0002:221-258); the two inducible fixtures are named in the acceptance, and the expired branch is checked in code but recorded as the branch no test can induce.

Recorded — WHY THE VALIDATION GATE DOES NOT READ cw.run.overridden. Both cw.run.gate_open and cw.run.overridden are write-once (0005:110-114 with the immutability triggers at 188-214 and select+insert grants at 288-291); nothing in the schema updates them. cw.record_override_gate() (0015:396-409) records that a gate was opened by writing a human_override_gate audit event and opens nothing. The only durable statement of 'this finding was let past' is cw.override_passes. A gate written against cw.run.overridden would make every engine-blocked run permanently unexecutable no matter what Legal approved, and WP-U10's whole workflow would terminate in an audit row. This paragraph belongs in executions.py, not only in the package.

Recorded — the window is not re-checked here. cw.override_passes joins the socialisation row and requires decision = 'approved', and cw.decide_override_finding refuses any decision taken before window_closes (0015:314-318), so an approved finding cannot exist before its window closed. Re-implementing the window in the endpoint would be a second copy of a rule the schema already enforces.

Decision recorded — ENDPOINT OR TRIGGER for the gates: endpoint, with the comparison written down so the next author has a rule rather than a precedent. Hard constraint 2 governs WHO may act; these gates govern WHETHER an act is currently valid, which is business validity and not permission. The database still decides who may file (0006 legal_writes) and the endpoint adds nothing to that. If a later owner wants the gates in a trigger, the code moves wholesale and the tests move with it.

Decision recorded — WHAT storage_uri CARRIES BEFORE WS-8. cw.executed_document.storage_uri is NOT NULL (0006:73) and no byte store exists. The endpoint requires the caller to supply it and writes it verbatim; the package records the synthetic scheme used in development under the placeholder-content rule, adds a comment beside the field list, and states explicitly that the POST /health-checks/document round trip is NOT claimed to work until WS-8 exists. Nothing here invents a location on the caller's behalf.

Do not split this package. A half-built execute endpoint that files an agreement with one of its gates missing is a worse failure mode than a large package, and the freeze triggers make it unrecoverable.

acceptance_criteria: A requester, a viewer and an auditor calling POST /agreements/execute are refused BY THE DATABASE (0006 grants and legal_writes policies), not by the endpoint; a legal_reviewer and a legal_admin succeed.

A run recorded against a different deal cannot be filed against this one — the refusal names both agreements — and a run with no deal cannot be filed at all, with the settled 'every assembly run belongs to a deal' decision named as the reason.

Execution refuses a run carrying a superseded or a retired clause, naming the clause and its state, with the fixtures named in the tests — a cw.supersession row with predecessor_disposition = 'retire_now', and a retired version. The gate's primary source is cw.clause_version_state; cw.run_drift is corroboration only and is never the gate.

Execution refuses a run whose gate is closed and whose blocking findings are not all covered by approved rows in cw.override_passes, naming the uncovered finding — AND admits a run whose gate is closed but whose every blocking finding IS covered, filing it, with cw.run.overridden still false. Both directions are tested and both are guarded by their own mutation row.

The mapping from a cw.run_finding row to an override_finding.finding_ref is stated in one function in executions.py as `{rule_id}@v{rule_version}`, matched with or without a leading `category:` prefix, and is fail-closed.
All three gates are evaluated BEFORE the cw.executed_agreement insert, proven by a refusal leaving cw.executed_agreement empty and cw.agreement.status unchanged.

The insert set matches what the hand-inserted demo row inserted and includes cw.executed_document.kind = 'agreement' at doc_seq 0; cw.signature_certificate is never written and a certificate in the body is refused with a reason.
The agreement's status moves to 'executed' by the existing trigger and never by the endpoint; executions.py contains no update of cw.agreement.
Exactly one agreement_executed event exists per execution and it is the trigger's; the endpoint writes only execution_attempted / execution_refused.
GET /reading-room/clauses returns rows for the first time, against a real executed agreement whose run_id is set plus a live cw.agreement_share row for a viewer — and no fixture fakes the run.

What storage_uri carries pre-WS-8 is recorded in the package and beside the field list, with an explicit non-claim about POST /health-checks/document; the endpoint-versus-trigger comparison is written down; the untestable expiry branch and the write-once nature of cw.run.gate_open / overridden are recorded in executions.py.
All four mutation rows report 'ok'.
npm run verify from backend/ is green, including all three mutation harnesses.
risks: The validation gate is the package's subtlest surface: read the wrong column and the endpoint is either permanently closed (cw.run.overridden) or vacuously open. Mitigated by the recorded paragraph, the positive-direction test, and the mutation row that breaks the override lookup specifically.

The finding-reference mapping is a convention, not a foreign key, so a mismatch between what the override form writes and what the gate expects refuses a legitimate execution. Mitigated by fail-closed matching, one function owning the spelling, WP-007 emitting the same reference, and the positive test constructing the reference through that function rather than by hand.

cw.run_drift is documented REPORTING ONLY, inner-joins cw.agreement, filters status <> 'executed' and emits only already-flagged rows. Mitigated by demoting it to corroboration and making the direct cw.clause_version_state query the gate.
Evaluating a gate after the insert would make it vacuous forever, and the failure is invisible. Mitigated by the ordering comment, the mutation rows, and the after-refusal emptiness assertion.

Everything this endpoint files is frozen by trigger (0006). A wrong insert cannot be corrected, only superseded. Mitigated by validating every field at the boundary and by running the whole flow against a throwaway schema in tests.

storage_uri will look like a real location to every later reader including cw.execution_evidence_gap. Mitigated by recording the value's shape and meaning in the package and in a comment, and by explicitly not claiming the document hash check round-trips.

Four new mutation rows key on code inside the same file this package writes; an in-package refactor turns them into fatal SKIPs. Mitigated by copying the find strings out of the finished file and re-running the harness at package close.
rollback_or_remediation: Code-only rollback: delete backend/doorway/executions.py and backend/doorway/test_executions.py, remove the dispatch branch and the four mutation rows, and revert the executed.test.mjs additions.

Nothing filed can be unfiled. cw.executed_agreement, cw.executed_document and cw.executed_signatory all carry frozen/no_delete/no_truncate triggers (0006), so any test filings must live in throwaway schemas — which the doorway fixtures already guarantee (the schema is rebuilt per test) and which the JS suites do by using PGlite.

If the gates must move into triggers later, the endpoint's gate code and its mutation rows move together; a trigger plus an endpoint check is two copies of one rule and is the drift this repo names as the vulnerability.

Settled decision 2 requires only the hash and the signatories at filing, which WP-006 delivers, so this blocks nothing in WS-1. Whether the act belongs to WS-8, to a new package, or to a later WS-1 addendum is a scope question only the owner can answer. Note the degree of freedom already in the schema: cw.signature_certificate.storage_uri is nullable (0006:322), unlike cw.executed_document's.

SECOND FINDING inside the same harness — its reverse check would not have caught cw.run_contract even after widening. views-are-not-policies.test.mjs builds its risky-table set by matching policy text for app_actor / owns_agreement / is_shared_with / was_notified, and cw.run_decision's read policy scopes transitively through cw.run (0005_run_store.sql:279-280) without naming any of them. NEW FOLLOW-ON created by WP-006's finding-reference rule, needing an owner — cw.override_socialisation resolves category watchers by matching `split_part(finding_ref, ':', 1)` against cw.override_watcher.category_key (0015_override_request.sql:220-228). Whether the canonical reference should carry a category prefix — and which category, given a finding may implicate several — is a question for whoever owns the override workflow. Both packages match with or without the prefix so a later prefixed form needs no code change here.

CORRECTION to an acceptance criterion the plan carried from its Part A prose — 'an empty library refuses loudly with SnapshotIncomplete's words' is unimplementable at write time. engine.run.SnapshotIncomplete (run.py:35) is raised only by snapshot_from_rows on the READ side; Snapshot.build accepts an empty clause list (snapshot.py:53-99); and a rungless ladder cannot arrive from the registry because LADDER_SQL inner-joins cw.ladder_rung (loader.py:56-67). WP-002 therefore tests the honest behaviour: an empty library is a 200 coverage-gap report in the engine's own words ('No clause available in Ledger'), with nothing invented and rules_consulted = 0. The refuse-loudly case that genuinely exists is snapshot_rows()'s ValueError (run.py:113-122) and WP-003 now handles it explicitly as a 409 with a named test, rather than leaving the guarantee in prose.

CORRECTION to WP-003's provenance-count decision (EV-420) — 'build the document in memory to compute provenance_counts' cannot be done without duplicating engine internals. engine.docx.provenance_counts requires an explicit `structural` list of build_docx's own literal strings (docx.py:403-415), and the only thing that constructs one is test code. Both alternatives — duplicate the structural vocabulary, or record both as zero — are recorded in WP-003 and switching costs one function, no migration. The owner may reverse it.

package_findings.issue: The currency gate's primary query is specified as `... join cw.clause_version_state s ... where d.run_id = %s and d.clause_id is not null and s.state <> 'active'`. Verified against C:\Users\MimoMac\repo\clausewerk\backend\db\migrations\0002_clause_registry.sql:246-262: `state` is set to 'superseded' whenever ANY cw.supersession row exists, but the sibling `selectable` column in the same view stays TRUE for a run-off supersession (`s.predecessor_disposition = 'run_off'` or `s.effective_on > current_date`) until the version expires on its own. The schema states this in its own words: 'A run-off predecessor is superseded but still usable until it expires on its own.' The gate as written therefore refuses execution of a run whose pinned clause the resolution engine itself still considers selectable — a false refusal in the one act that freeze triggers make irreversible. The package's own fixture (predecessor_disposition = 'retire_now') encodes the NARROWER rule, so required_changes and acceptance_criteria disagree with each other: this is a hidden unresolved decision about which states disqualify.
package_findings.correction: Change the gate predicate from `s.state <> 'active'` to `s.selectable = false` — the column the engine's own selection uses — or enumerate explicitly (`s.state in ('retired','expired') or (s.state = 'superseded' and s.selectable = false)`). Add a mandatory NEGATIVE test to WP-006: `test_a_run_off_supersession_does_not_refuse_execution` (fixture: a cw.supersession row with predecessor_disposition = 'run_off' against a selected clause; the execution SUCCEEDS). Restate the acceptance criterion as 'refuses a run carrying a retired, expired, or retire_now-superseded clause, and does NOT refuse one carrying a run-off predecessor still in force'.

EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE — the draft's evidence_summary is tagged throughout and its EV-5xx numbering stays distinct from the planners (EV-1xx/2xx) and the integrator (EV-4xx), as required. package_findings.issue: The validation gate is specified as `select gate_open, overridden, override_ref from cw.run where run_id = %s` and refuses when gate_open is false and overridden is false. Both columns are written once at insert and can never change: cw.run carries run_immutable no_edit/no_delete/no_truncate triggers (0005_run_store.sql:188-214) and holds only select+insert grants (0005:288-291), and no statement anywhere in migrations 0001-0023 updates cw.run (verified by grep). The entire human-override apparatus lives elsewhere — cw.record_override_gate() (0015_override_request.sql:396-409) only writes a `human_override_gate` audit event, and what an approval actually lets past is cw.override_passes, one row per individually approved finding (0015:364-374, rescoped 0019_override_views_scoped.sql:95-109). As specified, every run the engine gated closed is permanently unexecutable no matter what Legal approves, and WP-U10's whole workflow becomes a dead end that terminates in an audit row. The two named mutation rows cannot catch this: 'the validation gate is not checked at execution' still reports ok, because the negative direction still refuses.
package_findings.correction: Rewrite the validation gate against cw.override_passes rather than cw.run.overridden: read the run's blocking cw.run_finding rows and refuse only where a blocking finding has no matching approved row in cw.override_passes for that run_id. State explicitly in required_changes how a cw.run_finding row is named as an override_finding.finding_ref (cw.run_finding is keyed (run_id, seq) and also carries rule_id/rule_version; cw.override_finding.finding_ref is free text), because that mapping is currently an unresolved decision hidden inside the package. Keep cw.run.gate_open as the trigger for consulting the override tables, never as the answer. Add the positive-direction acceptance criterion and test — 'a run whose gate is closed but whose every blocking finding appears in cw.override_passes is admitted, and the execution is filed' — and a third mutation row or an extension of the gate row that keys on the override lookup, since the currently specified row proves only the half that already works.

package_findings.issue: Nothing in the required changes binds the run named at execution to the agreement being executed. The endpoint takes agreement_id and run_id as independent fields and inserts them into cw.executed_agreement, whose run_id column is a plain nullable FK to cw.run (0006_executed_agreements.sql:23-25) with no constraint tying it to agreement_id. After WP-003's migration 0024 a requester can only record a run against a deal they own, but a legal_reviewer or legal_admin can record a run against any deal or with a null agreement_id (the two-branch policy has no ownership term on the Legal branch) — so Legal can file agreement AG-2 citing a run recorded against AG-1, permanently, and cw.audit_executed will record it as legitimate. This also silently breaks the package's own test_a_run_with_a_null_agreement_is_still_gated, which after 0024 is constructible only as Legal, a fact the package does not state.
package_findings.correction: Add to required_changes: before the executed_agreement insert, refuse when cw.run.agreement_id is not null and differs from the agreement_id being filed, naming both in the refusal. Decide and record whether a run with a null agreement_id may be filed at all (the SETTLED decision 'every assembly run belongs to a deal' argues no). Restate test_a_run_with_a_null_agreement_is_still_gated as executed by a legal_reviewer, and say why that is the only role that can produce such a run after 0024.

package_findings.issue: The required changes read the run with `row = request.one("select run_id, agreement_id, vendor, value, manifest, snapshot_id, ruleset_id, result_hash, engine_version from cw.run where run_id = %s", (run_id,))` and then subscript it by column name — `row["snapshot_id"]`, `row['snapshot_id']`. db.Request.one() returns `self._cursor.execute(...).fetchone()` with no row factory set (backend/doorway/db.py:109-113), i.e. a plain tuple. Every subscript by name raises TypeError. WP-006's gate read of cw.run is written the same way. WP-003's use of one() (`... is None`) is correct, so the error is specific to the two packages that read columns back.
package_findings.correction: In WP-005 and WP-006, replace `request.one(...)` with `request.rows(...)` and take the first element (rows() sets column names from cursor.description, db.py:99-107), or index the tuple positionally. Keep one() only where the test is existence-or-None, as WP-003 does. State the rule once in the package so the next reader does not repeat it.

package_findings.issue: engine.docx.build_docx stamps the current date into the document — `today = today or date.today()` and `body.append(_para(f"Dated: {today.isoformat()}"))` (backend/engine/docx.py:113-123). The package therefore produces different bytes, and a different SHA-256, for the same immutable run on two different days, while asserting in its objective and out_of_scope that 'a pre-execution document is deterministic output of an immutable run' and recording sha256_of(the exact bytes) into document_produced as though it identified the run's paper. Two audit rows for one run that legitimately disagree is exactly the shape the repo's audit doctrine exists to prevent, and nobody reading the chain later will know why.
package_findings.correction: Record the fact explicitly in documents.py and in the package, alongside the two-hashes decision it already makes: the document digest identifies THIS RENDERING, not the run, and only the recomputed result_hash identifies the run. Then decide and record one of two options — pass `today=` derived from cw.run.created_at so a run's paper is byte-stable, or keep date.today() and say in the audit payload which date was stamped. Add a named test for whichever is chosen (two downloads of one run produce identical bytes, or produce differing bytes with the stamped date recorded). This also affects WP-003's provenance build, which builds a second document on a third date.

package_findings.issue: Migration 0024's rule (b) — replacing the role-only INSERT policies on cw.run_decision and cw.run_finding (0005_run_store.sql:281-286) with an `exists (select 1 from cw.run r where r.run_id = ...)` check — appears in required_changes as mandatory and in acceptance_criteria as a pass condition, while open_issues simultaneously records it as SCOPE GROWTH beyond what Gate 2 authorised and says 'If the owner refuses, drop rule (b) from 0024 and carry the gap as named'. A package cannot be both mandatory and conditional. As written the implementer cannot tell whether shipping without rule (b) is a failed package or a permitted variant, and the acceptance criterion 'a requester cannot append a run_decision or a run_finding to a run they cannot see' would fail a conforming implementation.
package_findings.correction: Resolve it before WP-003 begins, in the same conversation that puts rules (a) and (c) in front of the owner as a claim. Either (i) confirm rule (b), delete the open_issues hedge and keep the acceptance criterion, or (ii) move rule (b) to a named follow-on with an owner, delete it from required_changes and acceptance_criteria, and record the gap in 0024's header alongside the other discovered facts. Do not leave the package carrying both.

package_findings.issue: POST /runs ships in WP-002 with a body that has no agreement_id and a 200 answer carrying `"recorded": false`; WP-003 then makes agreement_id a required field refused with a 400 and flips the answer to `"recorded": true` with a run_id. The endpoint's request contract therefore changes between two packages, and WP-002 flags only the administrator-uniformity gap as temporary — not the body shape. Every test WP-002 writes against the two-field body, and any screen or script written against it, breaks in WP-003 without a stated reason.
package_findings.correction: Have WP-002 accept and validate agreement_id at the boundary from the start — required, refused with a 400 naming the field, and simply unused because nothing persists — so the request shape is fixed in the package that introduces the route. Note in WP-002's implementation_notes that the database's ownership rule behind that field arrives in WP-003 and that until then the field is recorded in the run_attempted payload only. If instead the shape is meant to change, say so in WP-002's out_of_scope and in the recorded gap, next to the administrator note.

package_findings.issue: The signature-certificate insert is specified only as 'cw.signature_certificate ONLY when a certificate was supplied' and 'accepts a certificate only if one is supplied in a form the JSON transport can carry'. Neither the column set nor the transport form is stated. cw.signature_certificate requires provider, envelope_id, completed_at, certificate (bytea NOT NULL with octet_length > 0), byte_size and sha256, with storage_uri nullable (0006_executed_agreements.sql:320-330) — and backend/doorway/server.py reads JSON only under MAX_BODY = 1_000_000 (server.py:56). 'A form the JSON transport can carry' is an unresolved decision sitting inside required_changes, in the one package whose every insert is frozen by trigger the moment it lands.
package_findings.correction: Either enumerate the field list and the encoding (base64 into bytea, with the 1MB cap stated and a refusal that names it when exceeded) and add a named test, or move the certificate out of WP-006 entirely into the already-recorded byte-transport follow-on and state that POST /agreements/execute never writes cw.signature_certificate. The second is the cleaner cut and matches settled decision 2, which requires only the hash and the signatories at filing.

package_findings.issue: The implementation notes correctly relocate the plan's 'refuse loudly' guarantee — 'The refuse-loudly case that genuinely exists at write time is snapshot_rows()'s ValueError (run.py:119-122) and it lives in WP-003' — but no WP-003 required change, test or acceptance criterion names it. A guarantee that Gate 2 listed as an acceptance criterion is therefore moved into prose and dropped, in the same set that argues at length against exactly that failure mode.
package_findings.correction: Add a named test to WP-003 (a snapshot containing a rungless ladder refuses with run.py's own sentence and leaves cw.run empty) and a matching acceptance line, or retire the guarantee explicitly with the reason that LADDER_SQL's inner join to cw.ladder_rung (loader.py:56-67) makes it unreachable from the registry. Either is honest; silence is not.

package_findings.issue: Step 5 says to rebuild the manifest from cw.run.manifest via manifests.manifest_from and re-resolve so the result hash can be compared. cw.run.manifest stores the ALREADY-CHECKED manifest — risks filtered, severities coerced, with separate `dropped` and `coerced` arrays alongside (engine/run.py:170-202) — and manifest_from reads only `risks`, `vendor`, `value`, `source` (manifests.py:70-102). The package never says whether check_manifest must be re-run on the reconstruction. An implementer who re-runs it, reasonably, gets a Manifest whose coerced set is empty where the original's was not, and the hash comparison then refuses every legitimate download.
package_findings.correction: State the reconstruction path explicitly: manifest_from over the stored `risks` only, no second check_manifest, resolve directly against the rebuilt snapshot. Add one line to the round-trip test asserting the recomputed result_hash equals cw.run.result_hash for a freshly recorded run, so the path is proved rather than assumed.

package_findings.issue: The package's central guarantee — the attempt row is written through cw.audit FIRST, so a viewer is refused by the database before the engine's answer is ever reported — carries no mutation row, on the stated grounds that it is 'already guarded by existing rows (the manifests.py reword row at mutation_check.py:235-241 and the db.py identity rows)'. Those rows key on manifests.py's wording and db.py's identity binding; moving the audit write below the engine call in runs.py leaves all 24 existing rows green. This is precisely the class of guarantee doorway/mutation_check.py exists for.
package_findings.correction: Add one 5-tuple to WP-002 mutating the attempt write in runs.py (delete or relocate the `select cw.audit('run_attempted', …)` line) with expect `test_runs.py::test_a_viewer_is_refused_by_the_database_before_the_engine_answers`. The objection that WP-003 rewrites runs.py is already answered by WP-003's own commitment to re-run the harness after refactoring the file, and by preflight, which fails loudly rather than quietly on a stale pattern (mutation_check.py:354-367).

package_findings.issue: Two line anchors have drifted and one api.jsx claim understates the change. package_findings.issue: The required changes state emphatically that server.py learns nothing about Word — 'the content type travels on the Download object from app.py' — and explicitly decline to define a DOWNLOAD_TYPE constant there. package_findings.issue: All three reads are parameterless and unbounded: GET /runs/decisions selects every row of cw.run_contract the caller may see, ordered by run_id and seq. For an auditor that is every decision of every run ever recorded, in one JSON body, growing without limit. The parameterless choice is well argued and correct as a scoping control, but the package records only the scoping rationale and never the size consequence.

global_findings: Coverage against the source plan is complete and correctly placed. Part A → WP-002 (wire and refuse) and WP-003 (persist and audit); Part B → WP-004; Part C → WP-001 (transport, hoisted) and WP-005 (document); Part D → WP-006; Part E → WP-007 and WP-008; Part F is inside every package with no trailing test package. The service-level round trip is in WP-005 and nowhere else, named as distinct from db/test/writer-sql.test.mjs:273 and guarded against vacuity. The three mandated mutation-harness additions are each assigned to exactly one package: rebuild-before-build in WP-005, expiry re-check and gate check in WP-006. No duplication, no orphan.

Shared-file ownership holds. backend/doorway/app.py (WP-001, 002, 005, 006), runs.py (002, 003), doorway/mutation_check.py (001, 003, 005, 006), test_runs.py (002, 003), db/test/executed.test.mjs (003, 006), prototype/v4/app/api.jsx and both screen test files (007, 008) are each serialised by unconditional prerequisite edges. WP-006 and WP-007 can be in flight together and share no file, so the one fork in the graph is safe.

The package set contradicts itself about its own shape: EV-527 asserts 'The chain WP-001 → 002 → 003 → 004 → 005 → 006 → 007 → 008 is strictly serial, so no two writers of any file can be in flight', while the declared prerequisites put WP-006 and WP-007 both at WP-005 with no edge between them. The graph is correct and the evidence item is wrong. Fix EV-527 rather than the graph — a reader who believes the serial claim will either lose the only available parallelism or, worse, conclude the ordering is advisory and parallelise WP-005 against WP-006.

Migration discipline is sound. Exactly one migration (0024) is claimed, by WP-003 alone; migrations end at 0023, so 0024 is genuinely free; every other package carries a per-package check that backend/db/migrations/ gained no file. The header requirement (state both discovered facts, cite hard constraint 2 as why an endpoint cannot fix either) satisfies hard constraint 4. The two-branch policy shape is right and planner-A's single-condition form is correctly rejected: cw.owns_agreement is `a.requester = cw.app_actor()` (0003_ladders_and_concessions.sql:626-631) and would lock out both Legal roles.

The central Gate-2 finding is confirmed at source and correctly repaired. cw.run_contract (0005_run_store.sql:231-238) and cw.run_summary (:240-248) carry no WHERE clause of their own, are granted to cw_requester/cw_legal_reviewer/cw_legal_admin (:296-298), and RLS is ENABLED on cw.run/cw.run_decision/cw.run_finding only (:265-268) — so cw.run's read_scoped policy is never consulted through them. cw.run's INSERT policy is role-only (:276-277), deliberately unlike the SELECT policy three lines above. Both facts verified independently.

WP-003's decision NOT to widen views-are-not-policies.test.mjs's catalogue query is verified correct and better-evidenced than the Gate-2 instruction it deviates from. The harness's ghost check (views-are-not-policies.test.mjs:143-150) fails for any REVIEWED entry the cw_viewer-scoped catalogue does not return, so entries cannot simply be added; and widening to cw_requester drags in five unscoped person-scoped views owned by WS-6 and the concession family. The substitute — a named standing assertion over pg_get_viewdef for the two run views — preserves the guarantee inside WS-1's scope. Accept the deviation; it is surfaced, not slipped in.

Two corrections the draft makes against the approved integrated plan are verified right at source and should be accepted. (i) An empty library does NOT raise SnapshotIncomplete at write time: engine/snapshot.py:53-70 accepts an empty clause list, run.py's SnapshotIncomplete is raised only by snapshot_from_rows on the read side (run.py:262+), and the honest answer is resolution.py's own 'No clause available in Ledger'. (ii) engine.docx.provenance_counts requires an explicit `structural` list of build_docx's literals (docx.py:403-415) built only by engine/test_docx.py, so the split — ai_origin_chars computed via ai_originated_characters, authored_chars 0 by construction with the engine's standing assertion cited — is the only version that does not duplicate engine internals in the doorway.

Every mechanical claim spot-checked against the repo held. READS is exactly 29 with the assertion at test_reads.py:100; doorway/mutation_check.py rows are 5-tuples whose preflight checks both that the pattern appears exactly once AND that the named test function exists (mutation_check.py:354-367), while db/test/mutation-check.mjs uses {target, suite, name, find, repl, expect} with a test NAME string — a distinction the packages correctly draw; test_server.py has 22 tests; server._respond json.dumps unconditionally (server.py:178-185) and do_GET drops the query (server.py:78-88); requester.jsx's caption is at :338 and its NotBuiltYet at :343; cw.executed_document.kind is NOT NULL against a closed set with agreement_is_first (0006:63-83); cw_auditor holds select but no insert on cw.audit_event (0001:339-346) while cw_administrator holds both (0013:257); cw.run_drift inner-joins cw.agreement and filters status <> 'executed' (0022:186-201); and all four owner-reads-a-run-view tests (run-store.test.mjs ×2, writer-sql.test.mjs:264, executed.test.mjs:279) do run with current_user as the owner, for whom cw.app_role() answers null (0013:84-94), so they do break by construction under 0024 as claimed.

Hard constraints hold across the set. The engine is untouched and proved so by a per-package diff. No endpoint contains permission logic: the two Part D gates are business validity with the comparison written down, and every refusal is the database's or the engine's own sentence classified by refusals.py without changing it — subject to the WP-006 gate defect above, which is a correctness bug in what the gate reads, not a permission decision moved into an endpoint. Every read and write goes through db.as_person. `npm run verify` from backend/, including all three mutation harnesses, is the last acceptance line of every package.

Rollback notes are present in all eight packages and are honest about what cannot be undone: cw.run's immutability, 0006's freeze triggers, and the permanence of audit vocabulary in an append-only chain with no UPDATE or DELETE grant. WP-003's note carries the prior policy text and prior view definitions verbatim so a 0025 can restore all five objects. This is the strongest part of the set.
notes: Verdict is REVISE, not BLOCKED: the cut, the ordering, the file ownership and the evidence discipline are all sound, and every finding above is correctable inside the existing package text without re-cutting or renumbering. WP-001 through WP-005, WP-007 and WP-008 can be issued once the minor corrections land. WP-006 must not be issued until the validation-gate defect is fixed, because it would ship an endpoint that can never execute an overridden run and the package's own mutation row would report ok while it did.

Suggested sequencing of the revision: (1) fix WP-006's gate against cw.override_passes and add the run/agreement binding check; (2) fix the request.one() tuple error in WP-005 and WP-006; (3) settle 0024's rule (b) with the owner before WP-003 begins, in the same exchange that presents rules (a) and (c); (4) decide the build_docx date question in WP-005 and propagate it to WP-003's provenance build; (5) fold agreement_id into WP-002's boundary validation; (6) resolve the certificate scope in WP-006. Items (7) onward are the minors and can travel with their packages.

Two things worth saying to the owner before implementation, because they are consequences rather than choices: cw.run is genuinely write-once — nothing in the schema can amend a run after insert, which is why the provenance counts, the gate state and the override state all have to be read from somewhere other than the run record; and cw.record_override_gate() records that a gate was opened without opening anything, which is correct for an audit chain but means the only durable statement of 'this finding was let past' is cw.override_passes.

The set's honesty about its own limits is a genuine strength and should survive revision: shell.test.mjs is named as static analysis rather than a rendering test, the manual browser walks are labelled manual and not claimed as automated, the expiry branch of WP-006's currency gate is recorded as the branch no test can induce (cw.clause_version.expires_on is immutable, 0002:126-158), and the auditor-cannot-download consequence is recorded as a decision with a named test rather than left to surface in an acceptance sweep. Do not let the revision quietly upgrade any of these into claims.

One carried unresolved item is correctly scoped and blocks nothing: the owner of byte transport for a signature certificate attached after filing. If finding 7 on WP-006 is resolved by moving the certificate out of the package entirely, this open issue becomes that follow-on's whole subject and the package set has no loose ends.
